And in the third year of his reign he sent his commanders and men of valour”; and further on: “and with them Elishama and Jehoram the priests; and they taught Judah, having with them the book of the law of the Lord, and they went through the cities of Judah and taught the people. And the dread of the Lord fell on the kingdoms of the earth round about Judah, and they did not make war on Jehoshaphat. And from foreigners they brought Jehoshaphat gifts and silver and presents, and the Arabs brought him seven thousand seven hundred rams, and Jehoshaphat went on growing ever greater.” What do you do that is like this? Why, you have sent throughout your whole kingdom so that we should all spit on God's commandments and accept your decree, which tries to fight against the Lord's commandment.

Jehoshaphat sent the mighty princes of his kingdom; he sent his counsellors; he sent Levites and priests of the Lord, entreating that everyone in his kingdom should be a worshipper of the Lord, and that all with one mind should offer themselves as servants to God alone. He also sent the book of the sacred law handed down through glorious Moses, so that they would do nothing beyond what God had commanded to be done. You, however, are found not only to have attacked the law of the Lord, which commanded that the innocent and just man is not to be killed, but to have forsaken God himself, since you hold not the apostolic faith but the faithlessness of Arius. He turned an erring people from idols to God; you have tried to make a people dedicated to God into apostates, which is what you are yourself, that is, sacrilegious.

You have persecuted, and you still persecute, Athanasius, thirsting for his blood. But see what the Holy Spirit says in the ninth psalm, in which you seem to me to be described in particular: “He has said in his heart: I shall not be moved from age to age, without evil. His mouth is full of cursing and bitterness and deceit; under his tongue are toil and sorrow. He sits in ambush with the rich in secret places, to kill the innocent. His eyes look upon the poor. He lies in wait in secret like a lion in his den. He lies in wait to seize the poor, to seize the poor, until he draws him into his company. In his snare he will humble him; he has bowed himself down, and he will fall when he lords it over the poor. He has said in his heart: God has forgotten; he has turned away his face, so as never to see.” If you persist in this wickedness, will it not be fitting to say of you: “He has turned away his face, so as never to see”? So many are the deaths you have caused, Constantius, that when it is said in the tenth psalm, in the person of our people: “In the Lord I put my trust; how can you say to my soul, Flee to the mountain like a sparrow? For behold, sinners have bent the bow, they have made ready their arrows in the quiver, to shoot in the dark at the upright of heart,” you seem to me to be described there, together with the partners in your crimes. For we know that you Arians are the antichrists of our time. Or if you are not one who deserves to be numbered among the antichrists, judge for yourself, you denier of the only Son of God. The Holy Spirit says through the prophet: “The Lord is in his holy temple; the Lord's throne is in heaven. His eyes look upon the poor, and his eyelids examine the sons of men. The Lord examines the just and the wicked, but he who loves iniquity hates his own soul.” And you have resolved that he should be punished whom you yourself have not found guilty, except only in this: that because he resisted your blasphemy, he has been made guilty of death in your eyes. Hear the Spirit of God say: “But he who loves iniquity hates his own soul”; and yet you compel us to love iniquity rather than justice. If it is not unjust to condemn a man unheard, with you heretics as his accusers, then prove the catholic guilty. For when I find it further written: “He will rain snares upon sinners; fire and brimstone and stormy wind shall be the portion of their cup, for the Lord is just and has loved justice; his face has beheld equity,” I recognize that you and all who act with you in this affair belong here. Fire and brimstone and stormy wind will surely come upon you unless you turn to God, because that is the portion of your cup, you deniers of the only Son of God, you persecutors of those dedicated to his divine majesty, who, though you know that God is just, loves justice and loves equity, have resolved to condemn an innocent man and to persecute the Lord's most faithful priest. “Love the Lord,” says the Holy Spirit in Psalm 30, “all you his saints, for the Lord seeks out truth, and he will repay in full those who act with pride.” And you had pressed us to kill an innocent man and to share your pride. For you could not deny that you are proud, since you have laid deadly hands on the worshippers of God and have tried to destroy the faith of the gospel and to establish the heretical one. Had you not read in Psalm 32: “The Lord loves mercy and judgment, and the earth is full of the mercy of the Lord,” that you should order an absent man to be condemned? Recognize from these works of yours how thoughtless you are and how much an enemy of your own salvation. For although you remember that it is written: “Who is the man who desires life and loves to see good days? Keep your tongue from evil, and your lips from speaking deceit; turn away from evil and do good,” you nonetheless take no rest from doing the very things that God has forbidden you to do. This is to refuse to see good days; this is to refuse life; this is to ask that death be given to oneself. Since, then, you are one who runs to drink down eternal death, you seem to me to have been foreshown in Psalm 35 as well: “The unjust man has said that he would sin within himself; there is no fear of God before his eyes. For he has acted deceitfully in his sight, so that his iniquity and hatred may be found out. The words of his mouth are iniquity and deceit; he would not understand so as to do good. He has plotted iniquity on his bed; he has set himself on every way that is not good, and he has not hated malice.”

Consider what sort of man you are, most just emperor, since even the things that were said against Judas Iscariot and the people of the Jews are seen to have been said on your account. How could we, Constantius, condemn an innocent man on the advice of your pride, when we knew that it is written in David: “Show your mercy to those who know you, and your justice to those who are upright of heart. Let not the foot of pride come upon me, and let not the hand of the sinner move me. There all who work iniquity have fallen; they have been cast out and will not be able to stand”? What do you say? Is the mercy and justice of God such that men are condemned absent and unheard, and innocent men at that, whom it is not lawful to punish even when present? But what wonder if you ordered these things, a man who does not know God? What wonder if, ignorant of his mercy and justice, you commanded perverse, wicked and unjust things to be done? Could the words of the psalmist not turn you away from so great a crime, when he says: “There all who work iniquity have fallen; they have been cast out and could not stand”? Nor his words in Psalm 36: “Cease from anger and forsake fury; do not be envious so as to do evil, for those who do evil will be destroyed”? Since, reading these things, you have decided that the statutes of the Lord are to be counted as nothing, I therefore judge you to be the one of whom it is said: “The sinner will watch the just man and gnash his teeth at him; but the Lord will laugh at him, for he foresees that his day will come.” We count you among those of whom I see it said: “Sinners have drawn the sword, they have bent their bow, to cast down the needy and the poor and to slaughter the upright of heart. Let their sword enter into their own hearts, and let their bow be broken. Better is a little for the just man than the great riches of sinners, for the arms of sinners will be crushed.” You have been placed among those enemies of the Lord whom the Spirit of God describes further on: “The enemies of the Lord, as soon as they are honoured and exalted, will vanish, vanishing like smoke.” Consider at last that you, with all your loftiness, unless you correct yourself, will perish like smoke, since you are an enemy of God. I see it further written of you that unless you turn and repent you will come to nothing: “I saw the wicked man exalted on high and lifted up above the cedars of Lebanon. And I passed by, and behold, he was not; and I sought him, and his place was not found.” You are, I say, Constantius, the one of whom I see these words also spoken: “The sinner watches the just man and seeks to put him to death; but the Lord will not leave him in his hands.” The prophet, full of the Holy Spirit, says: “Do not be envious among evildoers, nor be jealous of those who work iniquity, for like grass they will quickly wither, and like green herbs they will soon fall away.” Yet you, Constantius, destroyer of God's religion, say: “Imitate me”? Who would imitate you, except one who wishes to wither away with you like green herbs? Who, except one who wishes to be blotted out by the indignation of God, since Scripture truly says: “Speak justice; judge justly, you sons of men,” and yet you rise up to slaughter an innocent man?

There can therefore be no doubt that you are one of those to whom the Holy Spirit says: “For in your heart you work iniquities; on the earth your hands weave iniquity. Sinners are estranged from the womb; they have gone astray from birth; they have spoken falsehood. Their wrath is like that of a serpent, like the deaf asp that stops its ears, which will not hear the voice of the charmers, of the enchanter who charms with skill. God has broken their teeth in their mouths; the Lord will shatter the jaws of the lions. They will come to nothing like water running away; he has bent his bow until they are weakened. Like melted wax they will be taken away; fire has fallen upon them, and they have not seen the sun.” You hear that you and your followers will come to nothing, just as those have already come to nothing whose imitator you have chosen to be. You see that you, persecutors of God's servants and deniers of the only Son of God, are compared to serpents and asps; and do you still not fear, and move yourself at last into the house of God? Do you, who are shown to be one of those asps, not shape yourself instead to trample the devil's head, so that you may be made worthy to reign among those whose glory John tells: “He came to his own, and his own did not receive him; but to as many as received him he gave power to become sons of God, to those who believe in his name”? Did you not know it is written in Psalm 58: “God of Israel, rise up to visit all the nations; have no mercy on any who work iniquity,” that you should order sentence to be passed on an absent man? Nor had you recognized the Holy Spirit both warning and rebuking in Psalm 61 with these words: “How long will you rush upon a man? Will you kill everyone?” “The fear of the Lord,” says Solomon, “is the beginning of understanding; but the wicked despise wisdom and discipline.” This is why you despise discipline and wisdom: because you are without the fear of God. This is why you are described in the sacred writings as wicked—wicked indeed, because not only have you yourself deserted God, but you also persecute so fiercely those who worship him. Woe to you, because you are found among those of whom I read in Proverbs: “My son, do not let wicked men lead you astray, and do not consent if they entreat you, saying: Come, share in blood with us; let us unjustly hide a just man in the earth; let us swallow him up alive like the grave.” What was it in the Arians, imitators of the Jews, that delighted you, Constantius, so that on hearing these wicked words of theirs you followed them in shedding the blood of God's servants? Why did you not listen to the counsels of Solomon, who says to you: “Do not walk in the ways with them; do not turn your foot to their paths. For not without cause are nets spread for birds. For those who are partners in murder store up evils for themselves. These are the ways of all who carry out wickedness, for by their own wickedness they take away their own soul”? And again: “As long as the innocent hold fast to justice, they will not be put to shame; but fools, while they are eager for insult, have become wicked and have hated understanding, and they have been made subject to reproaches.” You, Constantius, have brought these reproaches upon yourself; you have condemned yourself, you who, despising the commands of God, have resolved to cling to the Arians, disciples of the accursed Jews, together with whom you rightly still hear these words: “Because I called and you did not obey, and I held out my words and you paid no attention, but you made my counsels void and did not heed my rebukes, I in turn will laugh at your ruin; I will rejoice over you when sudden tumult comes upon you and overthrow like a storm, when destruction comes upon you. For the time will come when you call upon me, but I will not hear. The wicked will seek me and will not find me. For they hated wisdom and did not take up the word of the Lord, nor were they willing to heed my counsels, for they scorned my rebukes. Therefore they will eat the fruit of their own way and be filled with their own wickedness. For because they deceived the little ones, they will be slain.”

We would certainly have deserved to be slain along with you, and by God at that, if we had joined you in persecuting the man of God. But how could we have done so, we who knew that it is written: “Do not devise evil against your friend, against the sojourner and the one who trusts you. Do not practise enmity against a man without cause, lest he do you some harm”? Or would it not have been without cause if, as the insane fury of your fellow heretics had ordered through you, we had passed sentence of death on an innocent man? Woe to you, for I see it said of you, our persecutor: “An insolent eye, an unjust tongue, hands that shed the blood of the just, a heart that devises evil thoughts, and feet that hasten to do evil.” You have read: “My son, honour the Lord and you will be strong; besides him fear no other”; and yet you wanted yourself to be feared and God to be despised. For how could we have been found to fear God alone if, yielding to your threats, we had condemned a man absent and unheard, and one whom we knew to be just? Solomon says: “A deceitful balance is an abomination before the Lord, but a just weight is acceptable to him.” You, on the contrary, do not hesitate to command: “Condemn the man by an unjust judgment,” thinking right what is perverse. Solomon again speaks of you and those like you: “The ways of fools are right in their own eyes, but the wise man listens to counsel.” “Condemn Athanasius,” you say; and where you could not prevail by the cleverness of your detestable subtlety, you began to prevail by the force of your imperial power. Take, then, what is written about you: “The wicked man does evil with insolence”; and again, since by clinging to the Arians you have already strangled yourself with a noose, just as Judas Iscariot did by clinging to the Jews: “The law is a fountain of life to the wise, but the fool will die by a snare.” It is further said of you: “A reckless king will fall into evils.” Surely you have fallen into these evils, because by denying the only Son of God you have left yourself no wisdom at all, but have turned yourself wholly to folly, and that is what has made you slaughter those dear to God. It is written: “The wise man, by fearing, will turn aside from evil; but the fool, confident, mingles with the wicked.” Had you not read that it is written: “He who insults the poor provokes the one who made him,” that you should drag us along with you to kill an innocent man? For if God is angry with one who insults the poor, how much more with one who kills his priest! Had you not kept in mind what is written: “The beginning of a good way is to do just things; and these are more acceptable to the Lord than offering sacrifices,” that you should force us to do unjust things? And in another place too: “He who calls the just man unjust, and the unjust man just, is abominable before God.” We would without doubt be abominable if we pronounced you just and judged Athanasius, a man acceptable to God, unjust. “To admire the person of the wicked,” it says, “is not good, nor to turn aside the holy and just man in judgment.” You, who are seen to be described in the person of the wicked, say the opposite: “Condemn the guiltless, imitating my person.” And although you tried to compel us to do things that could have made God angry with us, we nevertheless urge you, the enemy of our safety, to become pious instead of wicked, healthy instead of sick, living instead of dead, religious instead of sacrilegious.

“How,” you say, “shall I be able to attain these things? By what means?” Stop persecuting the house of God; stop proscribing, deporting and killing his servants; confess yourself a Christian; curse along with us the band of the Arians, devised by the devil's contrivance; believe as we believe, who are bishops in succession from the blessed apostles; confess the only Son of God as they confessed him and as we confess him; and you will obtain pardon for such great

crimes. For you have read in Solomon: “Death and life are in the hands of the tongue”; and in blessed Paul: “With the heart one believes unto justice, and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation.” You remember that it is written: “A false witness will not go unpunished, and he who accuses unjustly will not escape”; and yet you dared to disown Athanasius. For we had no case to answer with the Arians, the colleagues of your sect, since the power of God had long ago forestalled [?] them, together with Arius, at Nicaea, at the time when the faith was set down in writing not only against your blasphemy but against all heresies. We had, I say, no dispute with those false bishops, enemies of God and your teachers, that we should fight once again against those whom God had once and for all driven out from his people. So now our reckoning is with you, because you have set yourself up as the author of the charge that Athanasius was guilty; and because we refused to punish him unheard, you, a man who knew yourself to be a false witness, began like a savage wild beast and monster to seek to punish us along with Athanasius, as though by your gnashing you could overcome the strength of God's servants. For although Solomon says: “The threats of a king are like the roaring of a lion,” yet your lion's roars will have no power against us. Why? Because you are the forerunner of Antichrist, and we are soldiers of Christ. Why? Because you, the persecutor of his religion, cannot conquer the men of God. Likewise in another place it says: “There is no difference between the threats of a king and the wrath of a lion.” What is that to the servants of God, who have resolved that no one is to be feared but God, and who remember that our souls have been placed in the hand of God? Your fellow Arians may fear your roars, since they are without knowledge of God and have by no means put on the armour of God. But we of God's household laugh at your lion-like roars. Why? Because, recognizing you as the beast whose roars you are described as having, we must rather laugh at you, seeing a rabid beast set in the form of a man, than fear you. But if you are not a beast hiding under the likeness of a man, tell us. You have read in Solomon: “Mercy and truth are the safeguard of a king, and the just surround his throne.” Since, on the contrary, a band of malignant Arians surrounds you, and we see that you punish mercy and curse truth, what else shall we judge you to be but a wild beast and a monster? You are roused against us like a roaring lion because we love mercy and truth, because we have not punished an innocent and just man; and do you think that you are not a savage wild beast and a most cruel monster?

But what intention led you to commit these things I simply cannot see: that you should have hounded to such ruin a catholic bishop of complete righteousness, a priest of the Lord. Did you not remember that it is written: "To do justice and to be truthful pleases God more than the blood of sacrifices"? Athanasius displeases you. Why? Because he guards the tradition of the blessed apostles, because he confesses himself a Christian, because he refuses to be your fellow apostate. It is no wonder, since we hold to what is written: "But the holy man is unclean in the eyes of the wicked." To you wicked men the one who pleases God is displeasing, and above all to you, rash and proud as you are. You are seen to be rash and proud from this: you have stretched out your hand against God's ordinance, you thought the apostolic tradition ought to be destroyed, and you decided that the bishops, under whose care you ought to have lived, should be brought under your rule. Understand, then, what you are, as you hear through Solomon the name that belongs to you, proud man: "The rash and proud man shall be called a pestilence." Pestilent man though you are, you cannot afflict us with your disease, because divine mercy grants us protection. In short, pestilent as you are, you tried to make us pestilent along with you; but he to whom we live dedicated did not allow your temptations to reach upright hearts. For scripture prompts us: "Rescue those who are led to death, and do not hesitate to redeem those who are being slain. But if you say, 'I do not know this man,' know that the Lord knows the hearts of all. And he who formed the spirit of all knows all things, he who renders to each according to his works." When against this you say, "Condemn the worshipper of God, abandon the apostolic faith, take up my faithlessness," this plainly shows you to be a pestilent man. God wants us to come to the aid of those who are in afflictions and distress. You, however, press those who ought to do good to do evil, and you do it by bringing to bear the things you think people may fear. Consider now whether there is not in you the disease called the plague. It is a disease powerful enough to make not only bodies but souls diseased: the souls, that is, of those who are willing to listen to you when you say, "Condemn the Lord's bishop, reject the faith the church has always held, and take up mine, which Arius handed down." Holy scripture says: "To stand in awe of a person in judgment is not good. And he who says the wicked man is righteous will be cursed among peoples and hateful to the nations. For those who rebuke will hope for better things, and the best blessing will come upon them." Yet you supposed that we could be overawed by your person and condemn a man whom even you knew to be innocent, whom you held guilty only in this: that he refused to deny he was a Christian.

Meanwhile, see what reward is promised us because we rebuke and reprove you as you keep to the road of death: "Open your mouth," says the prophet, "with the word of God, and judge all fairly; open your mouth and judge justly." And you say: "Condemn an innocent man." I do indeed keep in mind what the sacred scriptures contain: "Do not be proud before the king." But if you had been willing to stay within the bounds of your power and I had shown myself proud against you, I would truly have condemned myself as a transgressor of the law. Now, however, since we are telling the truth to a murderer and a sacrilegious man, we will certainly not deserve punishment as proud men. Rather, we will be granted heavenly rewards because we did not spare you in your error. It is written: "A whip for the horse and a goad for the ass, and a rod for a foolish nation." We rightly call you deniers of God's only Son foolish, since we see you engaged in such great sacrilege. For when I see it written that "as a dog that returns to its vomit becomes hateful, so is a fool who by his malice returns to his sin," I judge that it was said especially of you. Why? you ask. Because in your letters to the Alexandrians you swore that you would do no further harm to Athanasius, and now you seek to kill him. But you say: "My father had sent him into exile, and I had to obey my father's decrees." Suppose, as you wish, that Athanasius is a heretic. If he had rightly been sent into exile, why did you let him recover, against your father's decrees, the office of which your father had judged he was deprived? But you say: "It was done at the intervention of my brother Constans." Yet you could have answered Constans: "Unless he corrects himself, I cannot receive into my part of the empire a man whom our father proved a heretic." But you say: "I was afraid that war would break out between us." Then, since Sapor king of the Persians is now waging war against you, if he says to you, "Take up my religion and I will be at peace with you," must you, together with everyone living in your empire, go over to the religion of demons? For Sapor sacrifices to demons. You see, then, that you did not act as a servant of God when you received him and recalled him to his see, a man you remembered had been deported in the cause of the faith. First, you judged God powerless, as though he could not protect you while you protected the truth and resisted the heretics. Second, you wanted Constans to be favourable to you more than God. If you remembered that King Constans had become a heretic by favouring Athanasius, whom you already held proven sacrilegious, then you ought not to have put before God your kingdom, nor even your very life. For you yourself are witness to your own conscience that he was sent into exile on account of the faith which the church has always held and still holds, because he refused to condemn it, that is, because he refused to be an Arian. It does not escape you that this is why your father hated Athanasius, since you too see fit to persecute him on the same ground on which your father persecuted him. Let him only say that he is not a Christian, let him confess himself an Arian, and in your eyes he will be very wise and great. So you have fittingly been compared to a dog that returns to its vomit. You were already regarded as a Christian and not an Arian from the time you restored Athanasius, with such letters as you sent, to the people divinely entrusted to him. But now you stand proven an Arian, and in your desire to find room for your heresy you persecute a righteous man because he attacks it with all his strength; so you are rightly compared to a dog returning to its vomit.

Likewise you must rightly be compared to a dog that returns to its vomit for that outstanding deed of yours: you accepted the truth that Eudoxius of Germanicia was not catholic and issued letters against him to the people of Antioch, and afterward you began to defend this same Eudoxius as a teacher of truth, upholding his heresy as the catholic faith. Why so fickle, Constantius? Why are you bent this way and that in the cause of the faith, like a reed beaten by the winds? What wonder if you were so ready to condemn Athanasius and even to invite all God's priests to condemn him, when in your rashness you did not hesitate to do such things in matters of religion itself? You, most pious king, boiled over in your eagerness to shed innocent blood, as though you did not remember what is written: "The king who judges the poor in truth, his throne shall rise up as a testimony." But you thought yourself supreme for this very reason, if you went against the divine scriptures and did everything they forbid. You hate Athanasius because he is a Christian. Because he refused to be, as you put it, a disciple of Arius, you persecute him with the utmost hatred. But long ago the Holy Spirit showed what you would be toward him, saying through Solomon's mouth: "The righteous man is an abomination to the wicked man." Do not, Constantius, linger any longer in these evils; do not abuse God's patience. Remember what is written in Psalm 77: "The Lord was roused as one asleep, like a mighty man drunk with wine, and he struck all his enemies in the hinder parts; he gave them everlasting disgrace." And in Psalm 81 the Holy Spirit says: "How long will you judge unjustly and favour the persons of sinners? Judge the orphan and the needy, do justice to the humble and the poor. Rescue the poor, and deliver the needy from the hand of the sinner." You say: "Kill with me the man dedicated to God," wishing us to be counted with you among those of whom it is said: "They have not known nor understood; they walk in darkness." God commands us not to give unjust judgment, so that we do not, out of reverence for your face, sinner that you are, allow you to punish the man you are persecuting unjustly. God has commanded us to do justice to the humble, to rescue the poor and to deliver the needy from your hand, executioner. And you say: "Condemn the man whom God willed to be rescued from my sinner's hand." No wonder; you could not go against your own execrable decrees. The Holy Spirit says in Psalm 96: "You who love the Lord, hate evil." Yet your commands show that you are saying: "Love what is evil." For if in God's sight it is evil that an innocent man be condemned and sentence passed against a man who is absent and righteous besides, what else are you forcing us to do but what God hates? If, then, we do what God hates, we will certainly not be among those to whom it is said: "You who love the Lord, hate evil." You do not hate evil precisely because you do not love the Lord; but we refuse to do what God hates precisely because we love him. You do these things because you are not the servant of the one whose fear and love compel us to hate evil. Nor are you, the persecutor of his church, found within the Lord's church, so as to suppose that the prophet was speaking to you in the psalm, "You who love the Lord, hate evil," since in Psalm 100 he says: "He who acts proudly shall not dwell in the midst of my house; he who speaks iniquity has not prospered before my eyes." So it is not said to you, who stand outside, but to us: "You who love the Lord, hate evil." We hate the evil which you love precisely because you are not in God's church. For how can you claim to be in God's church, you who not only persecute the church but deny the very one who founded the church? Are you not proud? And can you dwell in the Lord's house as long as you persist in this arrogance? Who could rightly be called proud, if you can be judged humble, you who say: "Condemn an innocent man against the divine commandments, trample on God's precepts, and keep mine"?

But perhaps you do not speak iniquity, and you can be found among Christians: you, the denier of the Father, the denier of his only Son, the denier of the Holy Spirit the Paraclete, the founder of the Arian heresy, the destroyer of the apostolic faith! You speak no iniquity with your poisoned lips; you utter nothing unjust from that sacrilegious mouth! Did you not know that in Psalm 102 the Holy Spirit said of the Lord, "The Lord does mercy and judgment for all who suffer wrong," that you should order an unjust judgment? Whose commands is it right for us, the Lord's priests, to obey? Yours, when you have not yet been rescued from unclean spirits? Or the prophet's, through whom the Holy Spirit warns us, worshippers of the true Godhead, to avoid every kind of injustice? Had you not read, Constantius, what God said to you kings, "Do not touch my anointed ones, and do no evil to my prophets," that you dared to stretch out your hands against the house of God? David, full of the Holy Spirit, says in Psalm 105: "Blessed are those who keep judgment and do justice at all times." And you say: "Do injustice with me." You persecute Athanasius: the impious man persecutes the pious, the heretic the Christian. But tell me, I beg you, which of you can be acceptable to God? You, who deny the eternal majesty of the only Son of God, the builder and founder of a false religion, or Athanasius? You have read in Psalm 118: "Blessed are the undefiled in the way, who walk in the law of the Lord. Blessed are those who search out his testimonies, who seek him with their whole heart." So tell me, which of you seeks God? Which of you faithfully renders service to his majesty? You, who persecute Athanasius because he confesses himself a Christian, or he who wishes that you, his persecutor, may be rescued from the snares of the devil? You, the destroyer of the catholic faith, or he, the preacher of the apostolic faith? If you serve God, how is it that the Holy Spirit says further on: "For those who work iniquity have not walked in his ways"? You heretics, then, workers of iniquity, since you are not found in the ways of the Lord, plainly show by your works that you are on the way of the devil. Have you read: "Do not court death by the error of your life, nor bring on destruction by the works of your hands, for God did not make death, nor does he delight in the destruction of the living"? Or not? If you have read it, why did you command us to seek death for ourselves? If you have not read it, learn what you have been urging us to do. For you have chosen to share the lot of those whose crimes the Holy Spirit describes through Solomon's mouth, saying: "They neither hoped for the wages of righteousness nor esteemed the honour of holy souls; for God created man incorruptible and made him in the image of his own likeness. But through the envy of the devil death entered the world. Therefore those who belong to his party imitate him." You see that you are an imitator of the devil, placed in his party. You recognize that you are seeking death for yourself, you who refused to remain in the image of God in which God made you, but went over to him through whose envy death entered the world.

Hear, on the other hand, what great happiness Athanasius longs to attain, which is why he refuses to be what you are, an Arian apostate. Hear too what great blessedness has been attained by those whom you have already seen fit to kill because they called themselves Christians: "But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and no torment will touch them. In the eyes of the foolish they seemed to die, and their departure from the path of the just was reckoned a misfortune; they went away into ruin, but they are at peace. For though in the sight of men they suffered torments, their hope is full of immortality; and having been afflicted a little, they will be greatly rewarded, because God tested them and found them worthy of himself. Like gold in the furnace he tried them, and like a whole burnt offering he accepted them. And in the time of their visitation they will shine, and run to and fro like sparks through the reeds. They will judge nations and rule over peoples, and their Lord will reign forever." You long to kill Athanasius, thinking that if you slaughter him you can inflict eternal evil on him, not knowing what is written: "The righteous man who has died condemns the ungodly who are living, and youth quickly brought to completion condemns the long life of the unrighteous. For they will see the end of the wise man and will not understand what the Lord purposed for him and why he kept him safe. They will see and despise him, but the Lord will laugh them to scorn. And after this they will fall without honour and be an outrage among the dead forever, for he will burst them open, puffed up and speechless, and shake them from their foundations, and they will be utterly laid waste, and they will be in anguish, and their memory will perish. They will come in fear to the reckoning of their sins, and their iniquities will convict them to their face." You see among whom your lot has been placed; you see with what sort of men you have made yourself stand against the house of God. But Athanasius you will see among those of whom, as you may hear, it is written further on: "Then the righteous will stand with great boldness against those who afflicted them and took away the fruit of their labours. Seeing this, they will be troubled with dreadful fear and amazed at the suddenness of an unexpected salvation. They will say among themselves, repenting and groaning in anguish of spirit: 'These are the ones we once held in derision and made a byword of reproach. Fools that we were, we thought their life madness and their end without honour. How have they been counted among the sons of God, and how is their lot among the saints?'" Unless you take thought for yourself, you will say these things then, when you see yourself plunged into Tartarus. Then you will say what holy scripture says the persecutors of Christ's soldiers will say: "So we strayed from the way of truth, and the light of righteousness did not shine on us, and the sun did not rise on us. We wearied ourselves on the way of iniquity and destruction and walked through trackless deserts, but the way of the Lord we did not know. What did pride profit us, or what have riches and boasting brought us? All those things have passed away like a shadow and like a messenger running by." Athanasius, on the other hand, you will see among those whose glory the Holy Spirit tells, saying: "But the righteous will live forever, and their reward is with the Lord, and their care is with the Most High. Therefore they will receive the kingdom of splendour and the diadem from the hand of the Lord, for with his right hand he will protect them and with his arm he will defend them." You, on the contrary, if you persist in this obstinacy of mind, if you decide to end this frail life among the Arians, will be among those to whom the Holy Spirit likewise speaks through the prophet's mouth: "Hear therefore, O kings, and understand; learn, you judges of the ends of the earth; give ear, you who rule over multitudes and pride yourselves on throngs of nations. For power was given to you by the Lord and might by the Most High, who will examine your works and search out your thoughts; because, though you were ministers of his kingdom, you did not judge rightly, nor keep the law, nor walk according to the will of God. Terribly and swiftly he will come upon you, for a most severe judgment will fall on those who rule. For to the lowly mercy is granted, but the mighty will be mightily tormented. The Lord will spare no one's person, nor stand in awe of anyone's greatness, for he himself made both small and great, and he cares for all alike; but on the stronger a stronger torment presses. To you, therefore, O wicked tyrants, are my words addressed, that you may learn wisdom and not fall away." Then, Constantius, if you have not yet listened to us, you will see what in your unbelief you are now quite unable to see. You will see it then, when you have been placed among your fellow tyrants in those places of torment: not only that you loved unjust judgments, but also that you wished to destroy the house of God, that you showed yourself a denier of the Son of God, and that by your threatening power you decreed that the faith be preached otherwise than the prophets and apostles preached it. Nor will you be able to say, "I am not among those whom the Holy Spirit describes through Solomon," when you hear him say: "To you, therefore, O wicked tyrants, are my words addressed."

So you will not be able to deny that you are the chief of all your fellow tyrants, if only you look deeply into what you have done. "The keeping of the laws," says the prophet, "is the assurance of incorruption, and incorruption will bring you near to God." Against this you say, "Corrupt the law of God," just as you yourselves, our persecutors, have corrupted it. Who is so senseless as to want to be corrupted by you and perish for ever? Who would not want to come near to God by remaining in integrity? Why did you either do these things yourself or dare to compel us to do them? Had you not read that Solomon said to God in the book of Wisdom: "God of the fathers and Lord of mercies, who made all things by your word, and by your wisdom formed man to have dominion over the creatures made by you, to order the world in justice and equity, and to judge with uprightness of soul"; and again: "By such works you taught your people that the righteous must be humane, and you made your children to be of good hope"? Had you not, I say, found these things written, that you dared to provoke us to such great inhumanity? How shall we be children of good hope? How shall we show ourselves just and humane before God as his servants, when transgressors of the law are called neither just nor children of God? Understand, then, from what a good you wished to drag us away to death, and eternal death at that, since everyone who ceases to be among those whom God has called into the adoption of sons loses life and possesses everlasting death. Since, then, you Arians are inhumane, impious, cruel murderers, how can you be called Christians? And since you also deny Christ, the only Son of God, and confess that you have believed in antichrist, from where or how can you prove yourselves servants of Christ, when by your own profession you have shown that you are slaves of antichrist? For the antichrist in whom Arius believed is truly one of whom it may be said that there was a time when he was not. Our Saviour, Lord and God, the only Son of God, on the contrary, is not, as you would have it, Constantius, a creature, but the Lord of creation. He is eternal and beyond all reckoning, as is he whose Son he is. He did indeed put on perfect manhood in the last days from the womb of the virgin, but even after taking up manhood he is unchangeable, incorruptible, ineffable and unalterable, just as is he whose Son he is. Taking up manhood could not change him into anything other than what he always was, since he is in the form of God his Father, since the Son is equal to the Father, as the most blessed apostle declares: "who, though he was in the form of God, did not count it robbery to be equal with God, but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant." For the fact that he said, "he emptied himself, taking the form of a servant," does not mean that God, the only Son of God, could become something other than what he is, incorruptible, ineffable and unchangeable, since he always remains in that state of eternal greatness in which his Father also remains. But we certainly understand what "but he emptied himself" means: that although the Son is like and equal to the Father, he nevertheless willed to become man as well, for our salvation.

Since, then, you have received antichrist in place of Christ, because he is truly the one of whom it may be said that there was a time when he was not, with what face do you still resist Christians, if not with the face adulteresses usually turn on chaste women? You dared to try to lord it over God's people, to subject God's church, which fears his divine majesty alone, to your kingdom and your worthless rule. And you did this because you do not know that it is written of you tyrants: "For this reason undisciplined souls have gone astray; for while the wicked are persuaded that they can lord it over a holy nation, they are bound with chains of darkness and fettered by a long night, shut in under roofs, fugitives." You see now that you are among those persecutors of God's people of whom you have read that they are all bound together by one chain of darkness; and again: "They indeed deserved to be deprived of light and to suffer a prison of darkness, who kept your children shut up, through whom the incorruptible light of the law was beginning to be given to all for life." Or will you deny that you are holding God's bishops in confinement? And why are you holding them? Surely so that we may not preach the truth to God's people? Why do you keep us in prison? Why do you send us into exile? Only because you fear that, with the holy Scriptures revealing it, we will expose you Arians as ravening wolves, rabid dogs and the antichrists of our time. For the holy Scriptures prove from your deeds that you are not servants of God but plainly children of the devil. For if you are not one of those whom the holy Scriptures proclaim would come, then since you found it written in Psalm 131, "Arise, O Lord, into your rest, you and the ark of your sanctification; let your priests be clothed with justice," why did you want us to condemn a man in his absence? Surely so that we would lose the justice with which the Lord had clothed us. For since it says, "let your priests be clothed with justice," and you were pressing us to do injustice, what else would we have been, had we done what pleased your malevolence, but your partners in crime, fountains of all iniquity? We, that is, who would have laid aside the office of justice and taken up that of injustice to please you. You persecute God's house, Constantius, not knowing that in his house you persecute God himself. For the house of God is the church, in which the Lord dwells, as it is written in the same psalm: "The Lord has chosen Zion; he has preferred it as a dwelling for himself. This is my rest for ever and ever; here I will dwell, for I have preferred it." Since this is so, see that you are punishing yourself whenever you punish any of us, that you are persecuting your own salvation when you fight against God, and not us, in whom you hear God say that he deigns to rest. You, then, who try to violate the temples of the Lord, unless you turn back, will perish in the same way as those of whom David speaks in Psalm 135: "Who struck Egypt with their firstborn, for his mercy endures for ever; and brought Israel out from among them, for his mercy endures for ever; who divided the Red Sea in two, for his mercy endures for ever; and led Israel through the midst of it, for his mercy endures for ever; and shook off Pharaoh and his army into the Red Sea." Why do I find these things written, if not so that I should believe that, when you tried to crush me, my God could destroy you, unless you turned back, just as he destroyed Pharaoh, and would rescue me from your hands just as he rescued them from Pharaoh's power? For this is why he says at each of his mighty deeds, "for his mercy endures for ever": to show me that the Lord's mercy remains always with me, who serve him alone, but cannot be with you, since you are plainly his enemy, as Pharaoh was.

We refused to condemn a man in his absence; we refused to pass sentence, as you desired, against one whom we know to be innocent and whom we know to be a preacher of the catholic faith. Why? Because we Christians have set our hope on God, not on you and your perishable kingdom. We refused to take pleasure in the glory of your kingdom, for we await glory from him in whom alone we must trust and hope, as David teaches when he says in Psalm 145: "Put not your trust in princes, in the sons of men, in whom there is no salvation. His spirit will go forth, and he will return to his earth; on that day all their thoughts will perish. Blessed is he whose helper is the God of Jacob, whose hope is in the Lord his God, who made heaven and earth, the sea and all that is in them; who keeps truth for ever, who executes judgment for those who suffer wrong." We refused to join you in unjustly persecuting a man full of the fruits of justice, lest, when God had begun to take vengeance on you, he should take it on us as well. We did not do what you unjustly commanded us to carry out, lest we should come with you to that place described in Ecclesiastes: "And God will seek out the one who suffers persecution"; and again: "I saw under the sun the place of judgment, and there was the impious; and the place of the just, and there was the godly." We refused to be joined to heretics; we refused to lend you our hands to attack God's house; we refused to take up idolatry with you, to the insult of God; we refused to be mixed up in your sacrilege, lest we too should deserve to hear, along with you, what the priests, the people and the king of Israel, who had all forsaken God and turned to idolatry, will hear from the mouth of the prophet Hosea: "Hear this, O priests, and attend, house of Israel, and give heed, house of the king: judgment is against you, for you have become a snare for ambush and like a net spread out for the fowler's catch." You surely knew that it was written in the prophet Amos, when you gave your instruction, that is, your example of condemning an innocent man: "who made judgment on high and set justice on the earth." Violator of God's justice, were you ignorant of what the prophet Micah said of the princes of the Jews? "They did not lift up their hands to God; they coveted fields and plundered orphans and his house, a man and his inheritance. Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I know evils against the people, from which you shall not lift your necks." But when you see fit to proscribe, deport, imprison, torture and finally kill the worshippers of God, will no evil be visited upon you? We refused to be mixed up in your abominable deeds, lest, condemned with you to eternal punishment, we should hear what God says in Micah: "Hear this, then, you heads of the house of Jacob and remnant of the house of Israel, who abhor judgment and pervert all that is right, who have built Zion and Jerusalem in blood by your iniquities. Her judges judged for bribes, her priests gave answers for pay, and her prophets divined for money, and they leaned on the Lord, saying: The Lord is among us; no evil shall come upon us." Had you not yet read in this most holy prophet, before you ordered a man dedicated to God to be condemned: "With what shall I lay hold of the Lord, and take up my God most high? Shall I lay hold of him with burnt offerings or yearling calves? Will the Lord accept thousands of rams or ten thousands of fat kids? Or shall I give my firstborn for my impiety, the fruit of my womb for the sins of my soul? It shall be told you, O man, what is good; and what else does the Lord require of you but to do judgment and justice, to love mercy, and to be ready to walk with the Lord your God?" Nor had you found it written in Habakkuk, "The impious by power oppressed the just," that you should undertake so wicked a work, one that could make you impious before God? Again, had you not found it set down further on: "Why do you look upon the scornful? Will you keep silent while the impious devours the just?"

And therefore, seeing that you, impious man, had tried to devour a just man, we not only did not keep silent about your wrongdoing, but neither shall we keep silent. For you are none other than the one of whom it is said: "The self-satisfied scorner, the proud man, will achieve nothing, who has opened his soul wide like hell." Nothing can be said that it would not be fitting to say of you, if you will recall with me your wicked crimes and are not slow to go over the deaths you have caused. For who else in our days can be found who is self-satisfied, scornful, proud, achieving nothing, who has opened his soul wide like hell and who could be thought as insatiable as death, except you? But see that God tells you that you can achieve nothing. For though you scorn God's commandments, though in your desire to persecute his religion you have opened your soul so wide to slaughter God's worshippers that throughout your whole realm you will not stop harassing the Lord's flock, yet all your hostility achieves nothing. For all whom you persecute are and always will be servants of God. But you, unless you look to yourself, will perish for ever: self-satisfied, scornful, proud, opening your soul wide like hell to devour and swallow us all together, because we resist you in your wrongdoing; you have become as insatiable as death, and you are driven by furies to kill us. You are so wicked, Constantius, that when I find the prophet saying, "O you who lay an evil foundation for your house, to set your nest on high," you, and the inheritance of antichrist whom you favour, come before my eyes [?], as I recognize those sacrilegious endeavours of yours. For there can be no doubt that you have tried, and are still trying, to have your heresy established throughout your whole realm and the catholic faith destroyed. And when I hear the prophet dedicated to God say, "Woe to those who build a city in blood and prepare a city in iniquities," you seem to me to be the one who is building a den of robbers by shedding blood, by slaughtering God's servants. Or will you deny that your malignant council of Arians is a den of robbers? If you are not robbers, how is it that you are found killing those dedicated to God? Woe belongs to those who build cities in blood. Most prudent emperor, did you not see that woe could be yours, since you thought your heresy must be rebuilt by shedding the blood of God's men? The Holy Spirit says through the prophet Zephaniah: "Seek the Lord, all you humble of the earth; do judgment and seek justice, and answer accordingly, so that you may be sheltered on the day of the Lord's wrath." You say: "Condemn an innocent man; be murderers and sacrilegious men with me." Are these not the things you command us to do? Did you or did you not command that a priest of the Lord be condemned? Did you command that the Arian perfidy be held and the faith written down at Nicaea be rejected? If you cannot deny that you ordered these things carried out, see that you wanted to make us both murderers and sacrilegious men. God says: "And on that day I will search Jerusalem with a lamp, and I will take vengeance on the men who are scornful, so that they do not keep the commandments"; and you say that your own commandments, and those of your fellow blasphemers, must be kept instead. How could we unjustly condemn a priest of the Lord full of the fruits of justice, when we see what threat arose against the leaders of the Jews and all their accomplices, who are known to have done the very things you are doing? "O city that was splendid and redeemed, the dove! She did not hear the voice, she did not accept discipline, she did not trust in the Lord, and she did not draw near to her God. Her princes roar like lions; her judges are like the wolves of Arabia, leaving nothing until morning. Her prophets are windbags, scornful men; her priests defile themselves and act impiously. But the Lord in her midst is just and will do no injustice."

Since this is so, and it is in no way lawful for us to pronounce an unjust judgment, it remains for you either to make yourself one of his servants and learn to pronounce judgment, or else, if you wish always to be among God's adversaries, to pronounce your unjust judgment alone, and to stop forcing us to do what you see is divinely forbidden. Stop now accusing Athanasius, or us, of destroying God's house, when you find yourself and your fellow tyrants described in Zechariah as future persecutors of God's inheritance, you who, he says, have seized power beyond all measure. For in describing your cruelty the Lord says: "I have been jealous for Jerusalem and Zion with a great jealousy, and with great anger I am angry with the nations that set themselves over you, because I was angry only a little, but they joined together for evil." Do you dare, lover of darkness and hater of light, to say, "Condemn an innocent man," when God sees fit to command us through Zechariah: "Judge just judgment, and show piety and mercy each to his brother. Do not use your power to harm the widow, the orphan, the stranger or the poor, and let none of you remember his brother's malice in his heart"? Since these are the commandments of heaven, on whose authority did you say, "Tear your fellow servant to pieces"? If you say you issued this order on the authority of God's commandments, you will not be able to prove it, since no command of God that an innocent man be condemned can be found in the holy Scriptures. Since, then, you have done what God's law forbids, it is clear that you issued this order by the will of the one who is known to be God's enemy. Hence you must be compared with those to whom it is said through the prophet: "They refused to pay heed, turned their backs in folly, stopped their ears, and made their hearts unpersuadable so as not to obey; they grew stubborn so as not to obey my law"; and further on: "They did not listen; they will cry out, and I will not listen to them, says the Lord almighty." "Souls, be at rest. These are the things you shall do: speak the truth each to his neighbour, judge peaceable and just judgment in your gates, let none of you devise malice against his neighbour in your hearts, and do not love a false oath; for all these things I hate, says the Lord almighty." Why do you force me to do the very things the Lord almighty says he hates? Moreover, when the Lord gives instruction about fasting, he says: "Love peace and truth." How could we be lovers of peace and truth if we punished as guilty an innocent man weighed down with false charges by you and your people? Or what peace would there be, when by doing this we could be cast out even from the Lord's peace? For the peace of the Lord who said, "My peace I leave you, my peace I give you," would not be left by him in us once we had unjustly taken it from another. Who does not know that when discipline departs, grace departs too? In Malachi God says: "A son honours his father, and a servant his master. If then I am a father, where is my honour? says the Lord almighty."

What fear and honour, then, were we going to show God if we had done what you ordered? Those orders of yours try to strip both the fear and the honour of God from those dedicated to his mercy. Further on, the prophet makes your work especially plain: "You have provoked God with your words, and you said, 'How have we provoked him?' By saying, 'Everyone who does evil is good in the sight of God, and he will bless them.' And where is the God of justice?" The prophet asks, "Where is the God of justice?" against those who say, "Whoever does evil is good in the sight of God, and he will bless them." And you give orders for the blood of the just to be shed, and you still call yourself God's servant, though you are the one wrecking his law. Is it just or unjust to condemn a man who is absent, and innocent at that? If it is not just, why do you force us to do the very thing for which God would rightly punish us? "All the days of your life, my son," says Tobit, "keep God in mind, and do not choose to sin or to break his commandments. Do justice all the days of your life, and do not walk in the way of iniquity; for if you act in truth, your works will be looked upon with favour, as will all who do justice." Tell me, Constantius: does a man who kills the innocent do justice? Does a man who sheds the blood of God's servants? If he does not do justice but rather iniquity, then you must see that you love iniquity and carry out every unjust work. The sacred law urges us to do justice at all times, and you compel us to do injustice. What else would you have me take you for but a lover and doer of injustice? "All the days of your life," he says, "keep God in mind"—yet you have abandoned him by clinging to the Arians. We who hold the apostolic faith do not abandon him. How are you not breaking his commandments, when you kill his servants who are dedicated to his name and majesty, and try to force them to forsake him and become your fellow serpents and fellow apostates? You hate us because we tell you the truth, because we want you to live with us for ever. But you love those who have gone over to you, those who at first opposed you but afterwards chose to serve your wicked schemes rather than obey God's commandments. You rejoice that by your cunning you have lured them into accepting your heresy, so that you now have wholly under your control the men you had long seen treating you as nothing, the men you saw trampling the authority of your reign underfoot with the truth. But we want you to know that this is nothing new. It has often been done by the faithless and the heedless, by those whom God, foreknowing the future, foretold through the most holy mouth of the prophet Malachi: "You have spoken harshly against me, says the Lord Almighty, and you said, 'How have we spoken against you?' Because you said, 'Everyone who serves God is a fool. What did we gain by keeping his commandments and walking in supplication before the Lord Almighty? Now we call strangers blessed; all who do wickedness are restored; they have defied God and been saved.' Those who fear God spoke against these things, each to his neighbour. And the Lord heeded and heard, and a book of remembrance was written before him for those who fear the Lord and revere his name. 'They shall be mine, says the Lord Almighty, as my possession on the day when I act; and I will choose them as a man chooses a son who serves him well. Then you will turn and see how great a difference there is between the just and the unjust, between one who serves God and one who does not. For behold, the day of the Lord is coming, burning like an oven, and it will burn them up. All the foreigners and all who commit crimes will be like stubble, and the coming day of the Lord will set them on fire, says the Lord Almighty, and it will leave them neither root nor vine.'"

You hear God say these things, yet you still choose to remain in your evil ways. I suppose you even rejoice that you will receive these things from him along with the transgressors and those who forsake God. Woe to you, murderer and blasphemer! Unless you repent of your deeds, you will remain what you are now, one of those whom God rebukes through the mouth of Isaiah: "Woe, sinful nation, people full of sins, evil seed, lawless sons! You have forsaken the Lord and provoked the Holy One of Israel." You will always be one of those whose wicked pursuits get them compared to the rulers of Sodom and the people of Gomorrah, as when it is said: "Hear the word of the Lord, rulers of Sodom; give heed to the law of God, people of Gomorrah." Unless you correct yourself, you will be with those about whom you have read: "Even if you multiply your prayers, I will not hear you; for your hands are full of blood." Woe to you, Constantius! You have offended God so gravely that you could not see what you ought to have guarded against. Through the mouth of Isaiah he says to those who murdered the holy prophets and all the just: "Wash yourselves, be clean; remove your wickedness from your enemies [?] before my eyes; cease from your wickedness, learn to do good, seek justice, rescue the one who suffers wrong, defend the orphan and vindicate the widow." Against all this you ordered God's worshippers to be slaughtered, God himself to be deserted, and idolatry to be embraced. Is that what it means to have heard God's warnings and been corrected? Why do you force us to do this, unless you want us to be devoured by the sword along with you? "If you are willing," says God, "and listen to me, you will eat the good things of the land. But if you are unwilling and do not listen to me, the sword will devour you; for the mouth of the Lord has spoken." Whom shall we obey: God, who says this, or you, his enemy? God tells the Jews to abandon their errors at last, cast the wickedness out of their hearts, learn to do good, and judge justly. You say: "Condemn unjustly." Why do you urge me to do this, unless you want me to become the kind of man God was speaking to when he said: "But you, says God, why do you burn my vineyard, and why is the plunder of the poor in your houses? Why do you wrong the people and put the needy to shame?" And these are exactly the things you are doing; this is how you carry on in everything. God is angry with those who do such things, yet you act as if you knew you could not please him unless you burned the Lord's vineyard, stored the plunder of the poor in your house, and wronged God's servants in many ways. Or will you try to say that you have done none of these things? Did you not burn the Lord's vineyard when you forced it to stop knowing the Lord of Abraham, the God of Isaac, the God of Jacob, the God of the apostles, prophets and martyrs, and to know instead the idolatry that Arius brought in and you have exalted? Is it not the plunder of the poor that lies in your house, the property of God's Christian servants? You have read it written about them: "Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven", and you know that you have confiscated the goods of those who resist your blasphemy. Will you dare to say, "I have not wronged God's people, and I do not wrong them now"? Who has ever wronged them as much as you, who never stop inflicting every kind of torment and every sort of punishment?

We refused to punish an innocent man as if he were guilty, so that we would not also be struck by the sentence that is prophesied further on through the mouth of Isaiah: "Woe to those who write wickedness; for those who write wickedness write it to turn aside justice for the poor and rob the needy of my people of their rights, so that widows become their plunder and orphans their prey. What will they do on the day of reckoning? For distress will come upon you from afar, and to whom will you flee?" We did not follow your poisonous advice, because in all our troubles and anxieties we want to take refuge in the one in whom Job, that lover of justice, took refuge in all his trials. We did not obey your cruel command, because we wanted to be found imitators of Job, the servant of God, who says: "I delivered the poor man from the hand of the mighty, and I was a helper to the orphan who had no one to help him. The mouth of the widow always blessed me. I was clothed with justice and covered with judgment; I was eyes to the blind and a father to the weak; but I broke the jaws of the wicked and snatched the plunder from their teeth." And further on: "I have been weighed on the scales of justice, and the Lord knows my integrity, for my foot has never strayed from the right way, nor has my eye looked [after evil]." What is this right way from which the glorious Job says he never turned aside? Surely it is the way that has never killed an innocent man and knows no other God, for it knows only the God of angels and archangels, the God you think cannot rescue us from your power. For you say of the faith of the blessed Church: "If the faith set down at Nicaea is catholic, let the one they believe in rescue them from my power." When you say this, you are plainly saying that God has no strength to snatch us out of your hands and cannot stand against you. You are claiming that the God of the apostolic Church does not have power enough to hold off your might. What else does the faith of the blessed Church confess, but that it believes in God the Father unbegotten, and in his only Son, begotten of the unbegotten and true Father, and in the Holy Spirit the Paraclete? What else does the faith of the Catholic Church confess, but that the Trinity is perfect and that the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit share one Godhead? What else does the faith of the blessed Church confess, but that it was not the Father who took on human nature, nor the Holy Spirit the Paraclete, but the only Son of God? What else does the faith of the glorious Church affirm, but that the only Son of God is unchangeable, unalterable, beyond reckoning, immeasurable and eternal, just as the one whose Son he is? The holy Church has believed that the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit have one power and a single dominion. This is the faith, I say, that you call heretical, while you claim that your own is catholic, the faith which says that God has no true Son, that there was a time when the Son did not exist, that he was made from nothing. You do this in the same spirit in which Rabshakeh, the general of the king of Assyria, taunted the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob, saying: "Do not let Hezekiah deceive you by saying that your God can deliver you from the hands of the king of Assyria." In the same way you, general of the Antichrist, say through your agents: "Do not let the words of your bishops, who oppose me, deceive you into thinking that the faith they preach can deliver you." They may vary the wording, but it comes down to this: plainly, you taunt us with God as being powerless to rescue us, just as the king of Assyria did: "Thus says the king of Assyria: If you want to be blessed, come out to me instead, and each of you will eat the fruit of his own vine and fig tree and drink water from his own cistern, until I come and take you away to a land like your own, a land of wheat and wine and bread and vineyards. So do not let Hezekiah deceive you by saying, 'God will deliver you.'" And further on: "Who will deliver Jerusalem from my hand?" But to Hezekiah, against a man such as you have shown yourself to be, God says through the mouth of Isaiah: "Do not be afraid of the words you have heard, with which the envoys of the Assyrians have insulted me. Behold, I am sending my spirit; he will hear a report and return to his own country, and he will fall by the sword in his own land." Now, Constantius, unless you look to your own safety, we see the same dangers surrounding you that surrounded the man who said: "This is what you shall say to Hezekiah king of Judah: Do not let your God, in whom you trust, deceive you by saying, 'Jerusalem will not be handed over to the king of Assyria.'" You are in danger just as he was, blasphemer, and you do not see it. We, on the other hand, the worshippers of God, see ourselves standing safe, protected and unharmed. Why are we safe and protected, if not because we hold the holy faith held by the patriarchs, prophets, apostles and martyrs, the very faith you have judged heretical?

But let us return once more to Athanasius, in whose person you are persecuting this sacred faith. Tell me, when you attacked God's bishop with false charges, did you not fear the anger of the Lord declared against those who tried to accuse Job, that most just of men? Are you not afraid, even now, that God may say to you what he said to the king who spoke against the most holy Job: "You have sinned, you and your two friends; for you have spoken nothing true before me"? You Arians may well be found superior to Athanasius in God's eyes now—exactly as those who accused Job were found superior to him then! It is in your interest, Constantius, to become a suppliant to God for your crimes through Athanasius, the Lord's priest, and to direct your prayers through him, just as those men did through Job. Make every effort to receive saving baptism through Athanasius or his fellow bishops. Twist and turn against Athanasius in whatever way you like: you heretics are found to be among the sons of that serpent, the snake, the runaway deserter. Athanasius, however, belongs to God's household, as Job did. He is one of the sons of light and keeps to the same way of justice that Job, the servant of God, kept. He possesses the faith, and that is why Athanasius is one of the sons of Abraham. Athanasius confesses the Son of God just as Job confessed him. Why is Job one of the sons of Abraham, if not because he believed as Abraham believed? If you do not know that this is so, read through the blessed apostle Paul, not only Romans but also Galatians, and you will find that what I am defending is true. Or will anyone deny that Job is one of the sons of Abraham just because the blessed apostle did not mention the righteous Job by name? If it cannot be denied that Job is one of the sons of Israel, there can be no doubt that he became so great a man, and the man he was, because he believed in God as blessed Abraham believed. The apostle reveals that believers are justified not by works of the law but through faith. His victory in those trials would not have been credited to him as righteousness unless he had believed in God as Abraham believed. How else could he have conquered the devil, unless he believed in God the Father unbegotten, and in his only Son, begotten of the unbegotten and true Father, and in the Holy Spirit the Paraclete? Or if you think that people did not always believe as we believe today, then prove that the blessed apostles and martyrs could have overcome your fellow executioners, conquered your friend the devil, and won the kingdom of heaven without believing in the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. So if those who believed after the coming of the Lord, the only Son of God, conquered by believing in this way, then believe that those who conquered the devil before his coming also believed exactly as we believe today. Daniel would not have overcome the lions, nor the three young men the fire, unless they had believed as the Church believes today. Finally, that is why the apostle appeals to the faith of Abraham: drawing on the authority of the sacred Scriptures, he proves that Abraham believed just as Paul himself now believed, and that Paul had been a child of wrath and in error during the time when he joined the Jews in denying the only Son of God.

Since this is so, I beg you to stop waging war against the house of God at last, and to accept the heavenly counsels that can lead you to eternal salvation. Hear what God says to you through the mouth of Isaiah: "Listen to me, you who have lost your heart, you who are far from justice." If your heart is still with you and you are not far from justice, why do you say to us, God's priests: "Condemn the absent, punish the innocent"? If you have not lost your heart and are keeping to the way of justice, why do you not observe what is written: "Keep judgment and do justice, for my salvation is near at hand and my mercy is about to be revealed. Blessed is the man who does this, and the son of man who holds fast to it, who does not profane my sabbaths and keeps his hands from doing injustice." And again: "There is no joy for the wicked, says the Lord." "Cry out with strength, do not hold back. Lift up your voice like a trumpet and declare to my people their sins, and to the house of Jacob their iniquities. They seek me day after day and want to know my ways, as if they were a people that had done justice and not forsaken the judgment of God. Now they ask me for just judgment and long to draw near to God." Wretched man, what hope can you have unless you repent of your evil deeds, when you hear God say: "There is no joy for the wicked"? Or will you deny that you are wicked toward the worshippers of God, when you do not deny that you shed blood? Moreover, God issued such rebukes against people because in the time of fasting they struck those under them with their fists and harmed them in other ways. What rebuke would he have issued against us if, against the commands of his divine majesty, we condemned a man who was absent, who had not been heard, and who was innocent besides? "Not even if you bend your neck like a hoop and spread sackcloth and ashes under you—not even then will you call it an acceptable fast." This threat shows us how great God's wrath against us could be if we condemned an innocent man. If the Lord is so angry when we strike those under us with our fists in the time of fasting, how much more if we were to slaughter his worshippers! If I may not strike those under me with my fists in the time of fasting, could I ever be allowed, at any time, to strike my fellow priest with the sword? "That is not the fast I have chosen, says the Lord. Rather, loosen the bonds of contracts made by force; set the broken free, and tear up every unjust bond. Break your bread for the hungry, and bring the needy who have no roof into your house. When you see the naked, clothe him, and do not despise your own kin." What hope do you have, most prudent king, when you turn all these things upside down? How have you loosened every knot of iniquity, when you remain in your unbelief just as you set yourself against us at first, and grow more and more malevolent in your efforts to destroy us? How have you done so when you, the author of blasphemy, have gone further in your blasphemy, even declaring by edict that it is the catholic faith? That is just how harlots behave: at first they fornicate in secret, but later they become so shameless and so lost to every sense of modesty that they want to fornicate in public. How have you loosened every knot of iniquity, when you still hold on to the fury you conceived against blessed Athanasius years ago, so that you want his blood shed? How have you set the broken free to rest, when you never stop torturing God's servants in one way or another? And how have you set the broken free to rest, when you see that prisons, mines and places of exile can now hardly hold all the Christians you have condemned? Even if you break your bread for the hungry, how will the Lord accept it, when you are starving to death the servants dedicated to his eternity? If you bring the roofless needy into your house, how will God deign to look on your work, when he sees the servants of his glory driven out of private homes and sent into exile because they refused to accept the idolatry that Arius established and you promote? If you clothe the naked, how can you please God, when you have stripped his servants of their inheritances and told them: "If you condemn the apostolic faith and accept the Arian one, you will get everything of yours back"?

Of all these holy commands of the Lord, you are found to fulfil just one: you do not despise the members of your own household. You certainly do not despise your fellow vipers the Arians, born of course of your shameless father, the devil. You love your brothers, because you see that they are closer to you. These you love with a special affection; on these you lavish all the glory of your kingdom; these you keep in your kingdom as your allies and partners in destroying God's inheritance. Them you have made rich; them you have raised above everyone placed in high office, namely those who have chosen to mingle themselves with your darkness. Since, then, you are doing the things God hates, how do you suppose that God can hear you, or that, if you give alms, they can be counted acceptable to you? For you hear him say: "Then your morning light shall rise, and your health shall quickly spring up, and righteousness shall go before you, and the majesty of God shall surround you. Then you shall cry out, and God shall hear you. While you are still speaking, he will say to you: Here I am." Do you suppose you can obtain any of these things, when no morning light has risen for you, but inescapable darkness has besieged your mind and the fogs of error have woven themselves all over it? What health has sprung up for you, when you lie in every wound of death, when every day you add to your wounds, when you are working hard to destroy yourself utterly? For us there is no health from any other source than, in the first place, that we have believed as the patriarchs, prophets, apostles and martyrs believed. How can righteousness go before you, when you remain wholly in unrighteousness, when you are the cesspool of the Arian doctrine, when you are a shedder of Christians' blood? How will the majesty of God surround you, when you are fighting against that very majesty, having chosen to forsake it and take up the idolatry of the Arian doctrine?
