How will you then cry out, and God hear you, and while you are still speaking say to you, "I am here," when you deny God the Father, deny his only Son, deny the Holy Spirit the Paraclete? How can he either hear you or say to you, "Here I am," when you are overturning his religion as far as lies in your power, when you have removed his catholic bishops and installed heretics? How will he hear you, whom you have thought fit to trample underfoot in every way, unless you repent of your evil deeds, unless you abandon your wicked ways and take hold of the right path of the holy Church? Then indeed you will be able to obtain these promises of God. For it is written for the sake of those who have turned to God with their whole heart: "Thus says the Most High, who dwells on high, holy for ever among the holy, whose name is the Lord Most High, who rests among the holy, giving evenness of soul to the faint-hearted and giving vindication to those crushed in heart: I will not be angry with you for ever, nor will I always exact punishment from you." But to whom does he say this? To those, surely, who have turned back by making amends, so as to blot out their sins. Hence also: "This is not the fast I have chosen, says the Lord; but loose every knot of iniquity, loose the bonds of forced contracts; let the broken go free, and tear up every unjust bond. Break your bread for the hungry, and bring the poor who have no roof into your house. If you see someone naked, clothe him, and do not despise the members of your own household. Then your morning light shall rise, and your health shall quickly spring up, and righteousness shall go before you, and the majesty of God shall surround you. Then you shall cry out, and God shall hear you, and while you are still speaking he will say to you: Here I am."

God will be present to you if, first, you believe in him, and then if you turn yourself to those things which he also says further on must be fulfilled: "If you take away from yourself the chain of iniquity and of bondage, and the word of grumbling, and give your bread to the hungry from your heart, and satisfy the humbled soul, then light shall rise for you in the darkness, and your darkness shall be like noonday. And your God shall be with you always, and you shall be filled as your soul desires, and all your bones shall grow fat, and they shall be like a well-watered garden and like a spring whose water does not fail." These things, as has already been said, you will be able to obtain if you come over to the Church, if you shun your fellow Arians, if you see fit to hate that congregation of the wicked of yours. Then God will be with you always; then light will rise for you in the darkness; then your darkness will be like noonday; then your path will be directed in good things. But if you persist in this obstinacy, in this cruelty of tormenting his servants, it will not be God who is with you, but the one who is found even today in your assembly of Arians, that is, the devil. For these things that you see fit to do are not of God but of the devil. If it is God's work that you proscribe certain [?] people because they would not condemn Athanasius, the innocent bishop of God, or because they would not hold communion with your fellow heretic George, or because they call themselves Christians and refuse to become your fellow apostates, then we may indeed reckon that your works are pleasing to God; and likewise that this is alms which you give out of other people's tears, out of the goods of those who preferred to be deported, killed and proscribed by you rather than either condemn an innocent man or deny the only Son of God, believing in whom, as they knew, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets, apostles and martyrs were glorified. That I long for you to become their companion and a sharer with them all, that these are my prayers for you, he is my witness who has the power to grant this to us
ON SAINT ATHANASIUS. BOOK II.

You dare, Constantius, to stretch out your hands against those dedicated to God and to harass them. Yet the apostle declares their happiness when he says: "We know that for those who love the Lord all things work together for good, for those who are called according to his purpose, whom he foreknew and predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son." Your persecutions do indeed work for our good. But mark what God promises you persecutors through Jeremiah: "Israel is holy to the Lord, the firstfruits of his generations; all who devour him shall repent of it. I will bring evils upon them, says the Lord." The evils that God promises you will come upon you, Constantius, unless you correct yourself, just as they came upon that carnal people, your fellow blasphemers, to whom it is said: "You have done evil so as to defile your ways, and in your hands has been found the blood of innocent souls." You will be forever among the enemies of God unless you truly hear his holy admonition: "If you truly amend your ways and your thoughts, and truly execute judgment between a man and his neighbour, and do not oppress the stranger and the poor and the widow, and do not shed innocent blood in this place, and do not go after foreign gods..." You will amend your ways if you now cease to persecute the servants of God, if you confess yourself a Christian and deny that you are an Arian, if you believe the Son of God to be the true Son of God, if you anathematize those who say, "There was a time when he was not, and he was made out of nothing." You will change your ways if you repent of your murders and of your sacrilege. Otherwise you will be, as you are now, one of those whom God reproaches when he says: "Is my house, in which my name is called, a den of robbers?" Whom do you hold to be the house of God: you Arians, or us Christians? For if your wicked congregation is the house of God, then a congregation of robbers is the house of God. For by shedding the blood of God's servants, as the Jews shed it then, you are seen to be robbers. By your fruits, Emperor Constantius, you are known to be no Christian, but plainly a ringleader of robbers. In short, you order the innocent to be killed, for you dwell not in the church of the Lord but in a den of robbers. You do not cease to kill those whom you see ready to be killed for the glory of the only Son of God and for his eternal majesty. We refused, at your false prompting, to pass sentence against a righteous man, lest this rebuke of the Lord should strike us too, together with you and with the Jews: "He has stretched out his tongue like a bow. In falsehood—and faith has not prevailed upon the earth, for they have gone forth from evil to evil, and they have not known me." You are both the contriver and the lover of false charges, and you do not know the Lord. Unless you correct yourself, you will be, as indeed you are, one of those of whom you have read it written: "They do not speak the truth; their tongue has learned to speak lies. They would not return, and they did not leave off usury upon usury, deceit upon deceit. They would not know me, says the Lord. Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I will burn them and test them, for so I will deal with them because of the wickedness of the daughter of my people. Their tongue is a wounding arrow; the words of their mouth are wicked. One speaks peaceably to his neighbour and keeps enmity within himself. Shall I not punish them for these things, says the Lord, or shall my soul not take vengeance on such a nation?"

Snatch yourself, Constantius, out of the pit of Arian madness, lest you pay eternal penalties with your partners in sacrilege. Do not glory in your perishable rank. Remember that you are mortal, for you cannot attain immortality in any other way than by acknowledging God and doing his will, as it is written: "Thus says the Lord: Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom, and let not the strong man glory in his strength, nor let the rich man glory in his riches; but let him who glories glory in this: to seek me, and to understand, and to know how to glory in God. For I am the Lord who show mercy and judgment and righteousness upon the earth, for in these things is my will, says the Lord." Since, then, you see that the Lord's will lies in these things, how can you see fit to loathe the very things the Lord says he loves? "Let him who glories," he says, "glory in this: to seek me, and to understand, and to know how to glory in the Lord." How can you now say that you glory in God? How can you claim that you seek him, when you are inciting all who worship his majesty to abandon the faith of the apostles and take up the blasphemy of your dogma? "Let him who glories glory in this: to seek me, and to understand, and to know how to glory in the Lord. For I am the Lord who show mercy and judgment and righteousness upon the earth, for in these things is my will, says the Lord." Since, therefore, you want an unjust judgment to be pronounced by the priests of God, and since you are a shedder of innocent blood, you are not the servant of him who deigned to speak these words through the mouth of the prophet. You are plainly the servant of the one who filled the heart of Cain, so that he killed a righteous boy, the first worshipper of the Lord. Hence it is that, though you are set in such exalted rank, you are nonetheless found to be one of those of whom, as you have read in the Gospel, the Lord said: "You are born of the devil as your father, and you want to do your father's desire; for he was a murderer from the beginning and did not stand in the truth." You are a liar and a murderer. You are a liar because you have brought false charges against Athanasius, the servant of God, and a liar because you call the heretical faith catholic and the catholic faith heretical. You are a murderer because you are hunting for the blood of Athanasius and have already killed a number of God's worshippers. Beyond doubt you have not stood in the truth, since you do these things. You are wholly rooted in falsehood, because your father too is a liar: he who drives you to deny the only Son of God, who urges you on to shed the blood of his servants. We refused to condemn an absent man, we refused to pass a harmful sentence, we refused to take up your heresy. We did not want to become like you and so deserve to hear what your fellow wanderers in error, the Jews, hear, to whose reproach, as we gather, it was said through Jeremiah: "All the nations are uncircumcised, and the whole house of Israel is uncircumcised in heart." Unless you surrender yourself to us, you are and will remain among those against whom the Holy Spirit cries out to God in the person of our people, saying: "I know, O Lord, that a man's way is not his own, nor will a man walk and correct his thinking. Teach us, Lord, but in judgment and not in anger, lest you make us few. Pour out your wrath upon the nations that do not know you, and upon the kingdoms that have not called upon your name; for they have devoured Jacob and consumed him and laid waste his pastures."

You see that you are one of those against whom the Spirit of God speaks in the person of our people. Unless you turn back, you can see that the wrath of the Lord will come upon you, the foreigner, upon you, the king, because you have not only failed to call upon the name of the Lord but have even persecuted. For when he says, "for they have devoured Jacob and consumed him and made his pastures desolate," who among your fellow tyrants can be found to be the chief destroyer of this pasture but you? You have not ceased to tear God's servants to pieces, nor to sow your blasphemies throughout your whole realm. There can be no doubt that you have tried to destroy the pasture of God's people, for you have taken away its shepherds. Of these shepherds, as we have often said, God spoke through Jeremiah: "And I will give you shepherds after my own heart, and they will feed you, feeding you with discipline." In their place you have installed heretics. On other catholics you have had a restriction imposed: if they wished to keep their sees, they were not to dare to preach the apostolic faith, nor attempt to teach the gospel tradition to the people while you, the defender of the Arian heresy, are still alive in the body. This is what proves that you have tried to destroy the pasture of God's people. For all the nourishment of Christian souls is nothing other than to believe as the patriarchs, prophets, apostles and martyrs believed, and then to fulfil all righteousness. You, on the contrary, have sought both to tear the faith out of the hearts of God's peoples and to plant your faithlessness there. You want it to pass for justice in God's church that an absent and innocent man be condemned, and that a catholic priest be punished by his fellow priests, men who follow justice, at the prompting of you, a heretic. How, then, can you seem anything but a destroyer of the pasture of the Lord's flock, since our pasture is nothing other than heavenly teaching? "If you wish," says the Lord, "to come to life, keep the commandments"; and again: "If you do what I command you, I no longer call you servants, but friends." This being so, if you would clear yourself, you must produce the commandments of the Lord which ordered that an innocent catholic bishop should be put to death by his fellow priests on the accusation of you, a heretic who happens for the present to be emperor. For perhaps at this point you will try to say that you have not attempted to destroy the pasture of the Lord's flock. If you cannot produce any commandment of the Lord like the one you have issued, it remains that the eyes of your heart, blinded by the blasphemy of Arius, should be opened by this rebuke from a servant of God and see that you have done everything we have charged you with. You cannot deny that you behave toward us just as that Herod behaved toward the little children who, as we read in the Gospel, were killed on account of God, the Son of God. You are found to be Herod's colleague in the frenzy of butchery, in sacrilege, and in royal rank. You have surely found the cruelty of Herod, which you now see fit to display, written in the evangelist Matthew: "Then Herod, when he saw that he had been tricked by the magi, was exceedingly angry, and he sent and killed all the infants in Bethlehem and in all its region, from two years old and under, according to the time he had learned from the magi." Perhaps you do not yet see that you have been moved against us, the worshippers of God, as unjustly as Herod was moved against those little ones. Why do you see fit to be hostile to us? Surely because we confess ourselves Christians, who have not condemned a righteous man weighed down by you with false charges. In these matters you can judge who you are from the words of blessed John the Baptist, and reconcile yourself to God through repentance: "Brood of vipers, who showed you how to flee from the wrath to come? Bear, then, fruit worthy of repentance, and do not presume to say, 'We have Abraham as our father.' For I tell you that God is able to raise up children to Abraham from these stones. For already the axe is laid to the roots of the trees; and every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire."

What do you think of this? Ought we to have condemned an innocent man? Ought we to have passed sentence against a man absent and unheard? And had we done this, how could we have been found to be Christians, when the most blessed John urged those people to bear fruit worthy of repentance so that they might become Christians? They had not yet grasped the way of righteousness and were being compelled to grasp it. We, who already hold to it, were being pressed by you, and are still being pressed, to take that road of iniquity on which the Jews are known to stand. What, then, could have become of us had we fed on your viperous counsels, except that from Christians we should have been turned into a brood of vipers? Why did you order these things to be done, unless you wanted us to become your fellow serpents? You know that the Lord said in the Gospel: "Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they will be satisfied. Blessed are the merciful, for they will obtain mercy." Yet you said that an innocent man must be put to death. How can I be blessed if I condemn a righteous man, if I reject the thirst for righteousness and take in a burning thirst for unrighteousness? How will God satisfy me for the fruits of righteousness, when this unjust deed makes me a Cain, a fratricide? How again can I attain the heavenly kingdom among the merciful, who are enriched with the fruits of mercy? If I kill a servant of God as you desire, I shall be found not merciful but cruel and wicked, a murderer in fact. And just as I was merciless toward my brother, so will he be toward me, that lover of mercy and exactor of righteousness who says: "Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they will be satisfied. Blessed are the merciful, for they will obtain mercy." "Whoever," says the Lord, "breaks one of the least of these commandments and teaches people to do the same will be called least in the kingdom of heaven." And you, Constantius, say that whoever has not shed innocent blood cannot attain the kingdom of heaven? Tell us, most holy one, in what way could the righteousness of Christians exceed that of the scribes and Pharisees, if we were to kill a man whom you persecute because he calls himself a Christian and refuses to become an Arian? In what way would we be better than the scribes and Pharisees, if we had joined you in denying the only Son of God, if we had repudiated the gospel faith with you as they repudiate it and had destroyed the apostolic tradition? Did you not remember that the Lord said, "You have heard that it was said to those of old: You shall not kill, and whoever kills will be liable to judgment. But I say to you that everyone who is angry with his brother without cause will be liable to judgment"? Did you forget it, that you commanded these things to be done? If I am angry with my brother without cause, if I call him a fool, the only Son of God says that I shall be liable to Gehenna. And you, Emperor Constantius, say that if I shed the blood of an innocent man I shall possess eternal rest? When you were planning that Athanasius must be killed, could you not keep in mind the condition on which the Lord commanded gifts to be offered? "If, then, you are offering your gift at the altar and there remember that you have something against your brother, leave your gift before the altar and go first and be reconciled to your brother, and then come back and offer your gift." What evil had Athanasius done, that you transgressed these commandments and ordered him to be killed? Surely only this: that he called himself, and calls himself, a Christian. For there is nothing else in Athanasius that you loathe and long to punish. Did you not remember that the Lord commanded us to love even our enemies? How then could you so fiercely persecute a man whom you knew had sinned neither against you nor against God? "You have heard that it was said: You shall love your neighbour and hate your enemy. But I say to you: Love your enemies, and bless those who curse you, and do good to those who persecute you, and pray for those who persecute you, so that you may be children of your Father who is in heaven, who makes his sun rise on the good and the evil and sends rain on the just and the unjust. For if you love those who love you, what reward will you have? Do not even the tax collectors do the same? And if you greet only your friends, what more are you doing? Do not even the gentiles do the same? You therefore shall be perfect, as your Father who is in heaven is perfect." The Lord commands us to love even our enemies, and you persecute us because we did not join you in shedding the blood of an innocent priest of the Lord. The divine voice cries out: "With the judgment you judge, you will be judged, and with the measure you measure, it will be measured back to you." And you say: "Cut the throat of a man you do not know to have done wrong." Though you remember that you yourself are the fountain of evils, you nonetheless dared to say of a man whom you knew your party was attacking falsely: "He deserves death." You are so senseless, Constantius Augustus, that when you commanded these things you could not even remember that saying of the Lord: "Why do you see the speck in your brother's eye but do not see the beam in your own eye? Or how can you say to your brother, 'Let me take the speck out of your eye,' when there is a beam in your own eye? And then you will see to take the speck out of your brother's eye." The Lord says that the beam is in your eye, and you dare to say to Athanasius, a most righteous man, "You have a speck in your eye"? For he has committed none of the things you see fit to charge him with. You, on the contrary, have perpetrated everything we have mentioned, as often as you have declared an innocent man condemned [?].

What other road did you want us to take but your own, which the Lord describes when he says: "How broad and spacious is the way that leads to destruction, and many are those who enter by it"? Because you are set on this broad and spacious way, you ordered an innocent man to be condemned, evidently wishing it to be revealed to all that your ruin holds sway far and wide. When you came to Italy, you, a wolf, disguised yourself as a sheep, as though we would not find you out by your works, and as though we had forgotten the Lord's warning: "Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep's clothing but inwardly are ravening wolves; by their fruits you will know them." Did not your most bitter fruits, sown in you by the poisons of the devil, show themselves at once in all their grimness, when you tried to say that a man unheard ought to be condemned? Were not your snares, ravening wolf that you are, laid bare at once, since you had built a mighty siege engine against God's sheepfold? By your fruits, then, you were recognized as a wolf and not a sheep. In the same way the holy Gospels prove that, unless you look to your own good, you are a tree destined for the fire: "Do people gather grapes from thorns, or figs from thistles? So every good tree bears good fruit, but the bad tree bears bad fruit. A good tree cannot bear bad fruit, nor can a bad tree bear good fruit. Every tree that does not bear good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire. So by their fruits you will know them. Not everyone who says to me, 'Lord, Lord,' will enter the kingdom of heaven, but the one who does the will of my Father." Is this how you do the will of the Father of the only Son of God? You deny his only-begotten Son and say that the Father himself is not a true Father. You try to destroy the foundations laid through the apostles. You have killed his worshippers and are killing them still. You have driven his bishops from the peoples entrusted to them, ordered an absent and unheard man to be condemned, and brought into the church your heresy, which blasphemes the one divinity of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. If all these things, as we have said, are pleasing to God the Father, then you will be able to enter the kingdom of heaven. For you hear his only Son say: "Not everyone who says to me, 'Lord, Lord,' will enter the kingdom of heaven, but the one who does the will of my Father." You order an innocent man to be condemned. Do you not recall that God said in Exodus: "If two men quarrel and strike a woman who is with child, and she miscarries a child not yet formed, the offender shall suffer a penalty: whatever the woman's husband assesses, he shall pay, as is fitting. But if it was formed, he shall give life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot, burn for burn, wound for wound, bruise for bruise"? I believe that nothing in the sacred Scriptures escapes you; for you could not give us such excellent commands unless you were learned in the law. You have surely read this too: "Everyone who hears these words of mine and does them I will liken to a wise man who built his house upon the rock. The rain came down, the floods came, the winds blew and beat against that house, and it did not fall, for it was founded upon the rock. And everyone who hears my words and does not do them I will liken to a foolish man who built his house upon the sand. The rain came down, the floods came, the winds blew and dashed against that house, and it fell, and great was its fall." Which of these do you say you are, Constantius, wise or foolish? If you say wise, why do your works show you to be foolish? Why is your house found to be built upon the sand? You cannot say that you have built your house upon the rock, when every wise man sees the structure of your folly and every servant of God beholds the great ruin of your salvation which the Lord foretold. For in what is a Christian found to stand firm, if not in obeying the Lord's commandments, and in remaining immovable even when harassed by every persecution for the name of the Son of God? In what will a Christian be made perfect, if not in being killed for him whom you see fit to deny to be the true Son of God? You, on the contrary, are not in the church but among the Arians, the enemies of God. You deny the only Son of God. You do not fulfil his commandments of clemency but rather try to destroy them. You are a transgressor of the law, a deserter from the oath of the heavenly army, a persecutor of God's religion, and you show yourself a butcher toward his worshippers. How, then, can you be found a wise man, like the one whom the Lord said built his house upon the rock?

But you reply to this: “I am not foolish; I know that I am wise.” If you are wise, why have you done, and why do you go on doing, things that only fools can do? If you are wise, why did you order a man to be condemned unheard and in his absence? Why did you command that an innocent man be put to death? Why did you want God's priests to become God's enemies? For they could not become God's friends by such a deed, since you know that the Lord said to the apostles: “If you do what I command you, I will no longer call you servants, but friends.” If you are wise, why must I, a priest of God, give heed [?] to you when you condemn Athanasius? Did you not refuse him any chance to set out the grounds of his defence? If you are wise, if you are a worshipper of God, why do you persecute us because we confess that we are Christians? Why do you so ardently love those who do not say that they are Christians but confess that they are Arians? If you are wise, why have you so often sent armed soldiers to the house of God? If you are prudent and know yourself to be God's servant, why have you persecuted his people with weapons, and why do you go on persecuting them? Why, finally, do you call the apostolic and evangelical faith heretical, and pronounce the heretical faith catholic? You call yourself wise; but we, on the contrary, see that no one who does these things can be wise. For what sacrilegious man could be called prudent, except by people more imprudent than himself? If you are wise, Constantius, I shall never be able to find anyone more foolish than you. Do you still think yourself wise, you who have judged that the prophets, apostles and martyrs were put to death for a creature? For you will not dare to deny that all of them were put to death for the only Son of God. How can you be called wise, you who not only made no attempt to withstand the falling rains, the flooding rivers and the blowing winds, so that they should not ruin you, who are shown to be the house, but have even turned yourself into rains, rivers and winds, so that you, a diabolical whirlwind and tempest, might drag us with you into the outer darkness? “Now the works of the flesh are plain,” says the apostle, “which are adultery, fornication, uncleanness, shamelessness, debauchery, idolatry, sorcery, enmities, quarrels, jealousies, fits of anger, brawls, dissensions, heresies, envy, murders, drunkenness, carousing and the like. I warn you of these, as I warned you before, that those who do such things will not inherit the kingdom of God.” And does your mind, so flourishing in wisdom, rage for the death of an innocent man? The apostle cries out that murderers will not possess the kingdom of heaven, and you, Constantius, the most prudent of emperors, say: “Cut the throats of the absent, slaughter the unheard, kill the innocent, and the kingdom of God will be yours.” From this we can see how wise you are, if indeed you are the one who built his house upon the rock. For you cannot deny that you said: “I wish to condemn Athanasius because I desire to please God.” So you wanted us, too, to please God in the way you yourself have pleased him, from the moment you saw fit to plot the destruction of Athanasius with all of us, the Lord's priests, as witnesses. In the same way, at the beginning, Cain pleased God as soon as he planned to kill his brother. In this way, Constantius, one sees where your root lies and from what stock you have sprung. After this, can you deny that you belong to that company which the apostle describes to the Romans: “And since they did not see fit to acknowledge God, God gave them up to a reprobate mind, to do what is not fitting. They were filled with every kind of iniquity, malice, shamelessness, greed and wickedness; full of envy, murder, strife, deceit and evil ways; whisperers, slanderers, hateful to God, insolent, proud, self-satisfied, boastful, inventors of evil, disobedient to parents, foolish, disorderly, without affection, without mercy. Though they knew the justice of God, they did not understand that those who do such things deserve death; and not only those who do them, but also those who approve of those who do them.” See what that excessive love for us, which suddenly sprang up in you, would have brought us if we had dared to go along with you: we would have drunk everlasting death. Again, further on, he says: “Repay no one evil for evil, but provide what is good not only in the sight of God but also in the sight of men. If it is possible, so far as it depends on you, live at peace with all men.” Thirsting to see these saving admonitions trampled underfoot, you urged us to punish an innocent man. For how would we have been found to provide what is good not only in the sight of God but also among men, if we had condemned an innocent man, and so set a pattern for shedding the blood of the just? How would I have been found to desire peace with all men, if, stirred up by the false prompting of you, a heretic, I had destroyed peace with my fellow priest?

Tell me, Constantius: was the charge you brought against Athanasius before the church of God true or false? If you are certain that the charge you brought was true, prove it to me, for I already know you to be the bearer of a false charge. Do you suppose you have done nothing evil in the sight of God? What reason drove you to become a false witness? Why did you prove yourself a lying emperor? Why were you not afraid of being struck dead like Ananias and Sapphira? Scripture, in the Acts of the Apostles, tells how blessed Peter said to Ananias: “Why has Satan filled your heart so that you lied to the Holy Spirit and kept back part of the price of the land? While it remained unsold, did it not remain yours? And once sold, was it not in your power? Why have you conceived this thing in your heart? You have not lied to men, but to God.” When Ananias heard these words, he fell down and died. And great fear came upon all who heard of it. The young men got up, carried him out and buried him. About three hours later his wife came in, not knowing what had happened, and Peter said to her: “Tell me, did you sell the land for so much?” And she said: “Yes, for so much.” “How is it that you have agreed together to put the Spirit of the Lord to the test? Look, the feet of those who buried your husband are at the door, and they will carry you out.” And at once she fell down at his feet and died. I believe you have read this, and yet you were not afraid to concoct a lie in the sight of the Lord. Why did you do it, unless because you are so wise? What do you think will become of you, who are not only a liar but a murderer, and not only a murderer but also a heretic? Do you believe such great crimes will go unpunished for you? Do you believe you can escape eternal punishment? To Ananias it is said: “Why has Satan filled your heart so that you lied to the Holy Spirit?” And will you say, Emperor Constantius, that Satan has not filled the heart of you Arians, so that you lied to the Holy Spirit who dwells in the church of God? For you addressed the church saying, “Athanasius has sinned against God”; and the Holy Spirit saw your lying souls, just as he saw Ananias and Sapphira. The Holy Spirit saw, I say, when you were fabricating these things, that you had invented such charges against Athanasius so that you could bring your heresy into the church and destroy the apostolic tradition. Ananias and Sapphira deserved to be judged in this way because, in selling their field, they kept back part of the price and dared to speak dishonestly before God's apostle. You have not only thrown false charges at a servant of God but have persecuted the whole house of God; you have shed the blood of his worshippers; you have sent his priests to the mines and into exile and installed heretics in their places; you have called the gospel faith heretical and your own blasphemy catholic; you have brought idolatry into the church; you have deserted the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, the God of Jacob, and of all the prophets, apostles and martyrs, and have followed the idolatry of Arius. Do you think that, if you persist in this blasphemy and cruelty, the heaviest vengeance will not fall upon you? Again, if God saw fit to take such vengeance on Susanna's adversaries, do you think a heavier one will not come upon you? It will, believe me, unless you turn back in time. For if those men, because they tried to violate Susanna's chastity, deserved to suffer what I have set out below, how much more do you, who have set about violating the chastity of the church? They assailed Susanna with a false charge, and you have assailed with just as many not only Athanasius but everyone who resists you. Or can you name a single one of those who resisted you to whom some charge was not attached? You were armed to violate the chastity of the church just as they were armed to violate Susanna's, when they said: “The garden doors are shut, no one sees us, and we desire you; so consent to us and lie with us. Otherwise we will bear false witness against you that a young man was with you, and that this is why you sent your maids away.” Or will you try to deny that it was said: “We Arians desire that we and you Christians become one body. Abandon the faith which you hold against us, written down at Nicaea, and accept the doctrine of Arius. Otherwise, since we are very powerful and the empire is ours, we will oppress you in whatever ways we please, and you will all be removed from your sees”? You cannot deny that this is so, since your schemes, hateful to God, have been exposed by the events themselves. For why were we compelled, even if we did not condemn Athanasius, nevertheless to join in communion with the Arians, unless because you, the pander of the Arian heresy, wanted all of us by any means at all to become your partners in sacrilege?

But I suppose you will still try to deny that the reason you persecute us is that we Christians refused to become Arians. How can you deny it, when you sent into exile the most holy Dionysius, bishop of Milan, who, believing your false assertions, had already condemned Athanasius, simply because he refused to be an Arian? Or is Auxentius, whom you in your rashness and pestilence ordained in his place, not an Arian? If Auxentius holds the holy faith set down at Nicaea, then you too may not be an Arian, and you may not have done all these things as I assert, and may not have brought a false charge against Athanasius. Perhaps you will say that you are catholics on this ground: that Susanna was heard, whereas we were not heard at all. As far as our own conscience is concerned, we know that we were vindicated at the moment when you, the serpent, were exposed, when all your poisons lay open, when your whole contrivance was laid bare. For this was the vengeance we desired on you enemies of God: that God should reveal to his people that you are heretics. Almost the whole world now knows that Athanasius was falsely attacked by you, and that you are the author of this iniquity; for you have been seen to want to accomplish one thing while professing another. Groaning, Susanna says to the people: “I am hemmed in on every side. If I do this, it means death for me; and if I do not, I shall not escape your hands. It is better for me not to do it and fall into your hands than to sin in the sight of the Lord.” We too, as soon as we saw the charges you had laid, stood to put out our own lamps, since then we would have been darkness, as you are. What Christian would not say that it is better for him to be killed by you, the forerunner of Antichrist, than to go over into the darkness of you Arians or of any heretics whatever? You had charges thrust not only upon Athanasius but upon us as well, because we Christians refused to become Arians. There was no lack of separate charges that could be brought against each of us individually, so that none of us would appear to have been sent into exile for God's sake, but as if for our own crimes. And so, though it is you who are guilty of such great crimes, because Athanasius refused to bring God's anger upon himself along with you, you declared him guilty and deserving of death. The elders, whom you equal in this wickedness, did the same. For Scripture says: “On the next day, when the people gathered at the house of her husband Joakim, the two elders came, full of wicked intent against Susanna, to have her put to death. And they said before the people: ‘Send for Susanna, the daughter of Hilkiah, the wife of Joakim.’ So they sent for her, and she came with her parents and all her relatives. Now Susanna was very delicate and beautiful. And the wicked men ordered her to be unveiled (for she was veiled), so that they might feast their eyes on her beauty. All her family wept, and so did everyone else who saw her. Then the two elders stood up in the midst of the people and laid their hands on her head. But she, weeping, looked up to heaven, for her heart trusted in the Lord. And the elders said: ‘As we were walking alone in the garden, this woman came in with her maids. She sent the maids away and shut the garden doors, and a young man who had been hiding came to her and lay with her. We were in a corner of the garden, and when we saw this wickedness we ran to them and saw them together. We could not catch him, because he was stronger than we were, and he opened the doors and leapt out; but we seized her and asked who the young man was, and she would not tell us. To this we testify.’ And the whole assembly believed them, since they were elders of the people and judges, and they condemned her to death.”

Consider carefully, Constantius, the accursed inventions of you Arians, and ask whether what you have done in the meantime against Athanasius is not exactly like what those men did against Susanna. For who would not have believed you, the emperor, when you said, “Athanasius has committed sacrilege”? But because in this you were more detestable than those utterly depraved false elders who are your companions, we gave you no credit. For you were told that an absent man could not be condemned. Those elders made their criminal allegations against a woman who was present, and the whole assembly passed sentence on her in her presence. You, on the contrary, when at the accusation of heretics you were forcing us to condemn a catholic unheard and in his absence, had already begun to let the machinery of your stage-play be seen. But now hear what the defender of the innocent and avenger of the oppressed granted to chaste Susanna. Hear what the book of Daniel relates about Susanna's vindication: “Then Susanna cried out with a loud voice and said: ‘Eternal God, who know what is hidden, who know all things before they come to be, you know that they have borne false witness against me. And now I am to die, though I have done none of the things these wicked men have invented against me.’ And the Lord heard her voice. And as she was being led away to execution, God stirred up the holy spirit of a young lad named Daniel, and he cried out with a loud voice: ‘I am innocent of this woman's blood.’ All the people turned to him and said: ‘What is this you have said?’ Standing in their midst, he said: ‘Are you such fools, you Israelites, that without examination and without learning the truth you have condemned a daughter of Israel? Return to the place of judgment, for these men have borne false witness against her.’” So now too, when Athanasius cried out to God, God made all his servants rise up for the truth against you, his adversaries. He granted his worshippers what he granted then to Daniel, his most devoted servant, so that we might understand that you are a false witness, that you are one of the brood of vipers, and that you made up these falsehoods together with your partners in sacrilege. Now all are returning to give just judgment, while you meanwhile hurl the sentence of death; even those return whom, in their ignorance, the devil, master of your soul, had ensnared with his cunning through you. For apart from your fellow Arians there can be no one who does not want God to vindicate Athanasius's innocence, no one who does not side with Athanasius's innocence, just as all now side with Susanna, once it became clear that she had been assailed with a false charge: the chaste by the unchaste, the pure by adulterers, the handmaid of God by servants of the devil. In the same way you serpentine sons of Satan have assaulted the standing of an innocent man who serves God faithfully; but you have been laid low. All your poisons lie dead, put to death by the power of God, since every Christian soul is entreating God that, as he did with Susanna, he would deign to rescue Athanasius from a false charge, to rescue him from your sword, executioner, from your savagery, murderer. Meanwhile I press you again and again to see what madness has seized you Arians, what insanity has gripped you, that you dared to contrive these things to bring about an innocent man's death, when you knew that God knows all things before they happen. But it is no wonder that you and your people built this contrivance against Athanasius, since you did not hesitate to say of God the Father: “He is not a true Father, for he has no true Son.” For when you say that the Son of God is from nothing, what else are you saying but that he is not a true Father? It is no wonder, I say, that you have risen up like this against Athanasius, the servant of God, when you do not hesitate to lay your deadly hands on him whose servant Athanasius is. For a robber who has not spared the master of the house will hardly spare the household that resists him.

But now let us return to what you ordered us to do. You said: “Condemn Athanasius.” What had prevented us from seeing him face to face? What had happened to stop me from examining every hinge of the matter? Why did you not allow him to be convicted by proper witnesses? Did even the most holy Daniel, or rather the Holy Spirit through Daniel, condemn those men without a hearing? For we read that the glorious Daniel said to the people: “Separate them from each other.” And he called one of them and said to him: “You who have grown old in wicked days, now your sins that you committed in the past have come home to you: you gave unjust judgments, condemning the innocent and letting the guilty go free, though the Lord says, ‘You shall not put the innocent and righteous to death.’ Now then, if you really saw her, tell me: under what tree did you see them together?” He answered: “Under a mastic tree.” And Daniel said: “Very well! You have lied against your own head; for the angel of the Lord has already received the sentence from God and will cut you in two.” Then, when he had put him aside, he ordered the other to be brought forward and said to him: “You offspring of Canaan and not of Judah, beauty has deceived you and lust has perverted your heart. This is how you have been treating the daughters of Israel, and they, out of fear, lay with you; but a daughter of Judah would not endure your wickedness. Now then, tell me: under what tree did you catch them together?” He answered: “Under a holm oak.” And Daniel said to him: “Very well! You too have lied against your own head; for the angel of God is waiting with a sword to cut you in two, so as to destroy you both.” Then the whole assembly cried out with a loud voice and blessed God, who saves those who hope in him. And they rose up against the two elders, for Daniel had convicted them out of their own mouths of being false witnesses; and they did to them what they had wickedly intended to do to their neighbour, in accordance with the law of Moses, and they put them to death. And innocent blood was saved that day.

What answer can your recklessness give to this, Constantius? You see that not even those guilty of so great a crime were condemned at random, but only after everything had been examined with the greatest care. And did you not hesitate to order the priests of God to pass a sentence of death on a man you knew to be innocent? What would we have heard if we had done it? Surely the very words that those reefs of lust hear, the false presbyters and false witnesses: "You who have grown old in evil days, now the sins you committed before have come upon you, judging unjust judgments, condemning the innocent and letting the guilty go free, though the Lord says: The innocent and the just you shall not kill." Would we not rightly and deservedly have earned these words, if you, the bilge of the Arian doctrine, had either enticed or frightened us into condemning an innocent man? And that is why all these evils have come upon you. You and your people are to hear what those men heard through Daniel: because you are guilty of bringing a false charge, because you invite the whole choir of bishops to put an innocent man to death, and because you wanted all God's people to take up your heresy. You will hear it, and more severely still, because your crimes are graver. You have shown yourself a destroyer of the religion of God. You have slain a huge multitude of those who call themselves Christians. You have brought your Arian heresy into the church. You have condemned the catholic faith. You have denied that God the Father is true Father, you have said that his only Son is not true Son, and you have asserted that the Holy Spirit, the Paraclete, is not the true Spirit of God. Yet against you and against all the enemies of God the faith of the holy church cries out that it believes in God the true Father, unbegotten, and in his only Son, born of the unbegotten and true Father, that is, of the substance of the Father, God from God, light from light, true God from true God, begotten not made, of one substance with the Father, which in Greek they call homoousios, through whom all things were made and without whom nothing was made; and in the Spirit, the Paraclete, the true Spirit of God. To you, then, false witness, spiritual adulterer, sacrilegious murderer, harsher words will deservedly be spoken, since by so many crimes of such a kind you surpass those false presbyters, the enemies of Susanna. For if it is said to them in their lying, "Rightly have you lied against your own head; for already the angel of the Lord has received the command from God and will cut you in two," and, "Rightly have you lied against your own head; the angel of God is waiting with a sword to cut you in two, to destroy you both," how much more will such things be said to you, unless you look to yourself! Had it slipped from that heart of yours, wrapped in the darkness of errors, that it is written, "Blessed are those who hear the word of God and keep it," so that you ordered an innocent man to be condemned? For unless I am mistaken, everywhere the sacred law speaks of not condemning the innocent and the just. And so, since you ordered these things to be done against God's command, we count you as one of those whom the Lord strikes in the Gospel: "Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, because you are like tombs that do not show, and people walk over them without knowing it." Those whom you enticed into loving you, sacrilegious man, did indeed not know it; because of your schemes they had not seen that you are a tomb full of all uncleanness. They took you for a man. But we, as soon as you began to lay on the bishops the obligation of condemning an absent man, said at once that you were a devotee of injustice and a persecutor of justice. And again, when we, as envoys of the blessed church, pressed you to condemn the sect of Arius, and you said instead that it was the catholic one, we declared in advance that you were the forerunner of Antichrist.

When you see fit to persecute Christians, when you kill them, you make yourself, Constantius, like those to whom the Lord says: "Woe to you who build the tombs of the prophets, whereas your fathers killed them. So do you bear witness that you do not consent to the deeds of your fathers? For they killed them, and you built their tombs. Therefore I send prophets and apostles, and some of them they will kill and persecute, so that the blood of all the prophets shed since the foundation of the world may be required, from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah, who perished between the altar and the sanctuary. Yes, I tell you, it will be required of this generation." That you are one of them is plain from this: though you restore the shrines of the blessed martyrs, you still shed the blood of the servants of the only Son of God. Come back, Constantius, to the house of God. Be a Christian, so that you are not found outside the church and remain forever, as you are today, among those whom the Lord strikes when he says: "Strive to enter through the narrow door, for I tell you, many will seek and will not be able. When the master of the house has risen and shut the door, and you begin to stand outside and knock, saying, Lord, Lord, open to us, he will answer, I do not know where you come from. Then you will begin to say, We ate and drank in your presence, and you taught in our streets. And he will say to you, I do not know where you come from; depart from me, all you workers of iniquity. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth when you see Abraham, Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets entering the kingdom of God, and yourselves thrown out." Do not hate yourself so much that you let yourself hear these words among them, especially since you see that you have been more wicked than one to whom it might fittingly be said, "Depart from me, worker of iniquity." If you choose to persist in this malice of yours, Constantius, you will be among that carnal people to whom it is said: "Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those who are sent to you." You will be among them, I say, because you persecute those who urge you to win God's favour, just as they persecuted the prophets and apostles.

Once more the defence of the truth compels us to ask you why you ordered an absent man to be condemned. Tell me, please: was it right or wrong for you to command this? If you say it was right, I suppose you will take refuge in what blessed Paul did, since he wrote to the Corinthians that he had already punished the sinner whom he had learned had gravely offended. Let us see now, you beast, who have only the limbs and body of a man but the mind of a wild animal, whether you acted as the apostle acted, whether you carried the matter through in the same order as he who said: "It is actually reported that there is fornication among you, and of a kind not found even among the Gentiles, that someone has his father's wife. And you are puffed up, instead of mourning, so that the man who has done this deed might be removed from among you. For I, absent in body but present in spirit, have already judged, as though present, the man who has done this: in the name of the Lord Jesus, when you are gathered together with my spirit, with the power of our Lord Jesus Christ, you are to hand such a man over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that his spirit may be saved in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ." I suppose you will say, "That is why I too ordered you to condemn an absent man, because the apostle also condemned one." First of all, the blessed apostle had been informed by catholics whom he knew to be faithful and had proved to be devoted to God, and he knew that the whole holy church of the Corinthians was a witness. You, on the contrary, you darkness, with yourself and your fellow sacrilegious men, heretics hateful to God, as the accusers, saw fit to press us to condemn an absent man. Next, when you hear the apostle say, "when you are gathered together with my spirit, with the power of the Lord Jesus, you are to hand such a man over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh," why, you darkness, did you refuse when we said, "We will go to him at our own expense; we will hear him among the people over whom he has been set by God; only provide catholic accusers, as the command of the sacred law requires"? Why, as though we were gladiators and not bishops, did you work only to have us do as you wished and kill the man whose blood you had long been thirsting for? Meanwhile you must know that you, wretched man, have been handed over to Satan for your murders and your sacrilege, just like the man who was found guilty of that offence among the Corinthians. For the deaths you have caused and are still causing are no lesser deeds; so if the Holy Spirit says through the mouth of the blessed apostle that he handed that man over to Satan for destruction, he must also have handed you over as soon as you committed such grave crimes. If it were not so, you would surely have remembered that the apostle said, "You were bought with a price; do not become slaves of men"; you would never have dared to force the priests of God to condemn a man unheard. For I was bought with a price: freed from the law of sin, I was made a slave of righteousness. Now that I live under the law of righteousness, you ought not to have laid on me a burden that would make me once again a slave of iniquity and injustice. So the burden was laid on me by you because you had been handed over to Satan for destruction on account of your murders and sacrilege. If you had not been handed over to Satan, you would remember that the apostle wrote to Timothy: "We know that the law is good, if one uses it lawfully, knowing this, that the law is not laid down for the just, but for the unjust and disobedient, for the ungodly and sinners, for the wicked and profane, for those who kill their fathers and those who kill their mothers, for the unchaste, for men who lie with men, for kidnappers, liars, perjurers, and whatever else is opposed to sound doctrine, which accords with the gospel of the glory of the blessed God that has been entrusted to me." If you were not handed over to Satan for destruction from the moment you denied the Son of God, how is it that you passed over so many things that could have held you back from so great a crime, and saw fit to rush into doing these things, which are capable of abolishing everything known to belong to sound doctrine?

You who do these things that are opposed to sound doctrine, you who proscribe, torture, deport, imprison and kill: tell me, I beg you, are you any different from that King Herod whose butchery sacred Scripture describes as follows? "At that time King Herod laid violent hands on some who belonged to the church. He killed James the brother of John with the sword, and when he saw that this pleased the Jews, he went on to arrest Peter as well. This was during the days of Unleavened Bread. When he had seized him, he put him in prison and handed him over to four squads of four soldiers to guard him, intending to bring him out to the people after the Passover. So Peter was kept in prison, but the church was praying most earnestly to the Lord for him. And when Herod was about to bring him out, that very night Peter was sleeping between soldiers, bound with two chains, and guards before the door were keeping the prison. And behold, an angel of the Lord stood beside him, and a light shone from him in that place. He struck Peter on the side and woke him, saying, Get up quickly. And he got up, and the chains fell from his hands." And further on: "When they had passed the first and the second guard, they came to the iron gate leading into the city, which opened for them of its own accord. They went out and walked along one street, and at once the angel left him. And Peter came to himself and said, Now I know that the Lord has truly sent his angel and rescued me from the hand of Herod and from all that the Jewish people were expecting. When day came, there was no small commotion among the soldiers over what had become of Peter. And when Herod had searched for him and not found him, he questioned the guards and ordered them to be led away." We see that you are like him in everything, whether in cruelty or in sacrilege. As he killed the blessed apostle James, so you too have killed a huge multitude of those who believe as the apostle James believed. As he persecuted the only Son of God in the apostle James, so you too persecute him, both in those you have already slain and in us. Again we both instruct and exhort you to return to the church of God and to stop persecuting Athanasius, and us who act against your heresy, so that you do not begin to perish after the example of this Herod, whose death sacred Scripture recounts, saying: "He went down from Judea to Caesarea and stayed there. Now he was very angry with the people of Tyre and Sidon; and they came to him with one accord, and having won over Blastus, the king's chamberlain, they asked for peace, because their country depended on the king's country for food. On an appointed day Herod put on his royal robes, sat on the tribunal, and made a speech to them. And the people kept shouting, The voice of a god and not of a man! And at once an angel of the Lord struck him down, because he did not give the glory to God, and he was eaten by worms and died." You who want to appear learned in the law, were you unaware, when you said, "Condemn an innocent man," that the blessed apostle John said: "By this we know that we have come to know him, if we keep his commandments. Whoever says, I have come to know him, but does not keep his commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him. But whoever keeps his word, in him the love of God is truly perfected"? You order things to be done against God's command; the apostle, on the contrary, says that whoever does not keep his precepts has not even known him, for, he says, if someone says, "I have come to know him," and does not keep his commandments, he is a liar, and the truth is not in him. You want us to be liars, you want us to be found murderers, doubtless for this purpose: that we may not be found to be Christians. For Christians are neither liars nor murderers. The apostle says, "Whoever keeps his word, in them the love of God is truly perfected"; and you, apostate and forerunner of Antichrist, say, "Whoever does not keep his commandments shall live." He goes on: "Whoever says he is in the light and hates his brother is still in darkness. Whoever loves his brother abides in the light, and there is no cause of stumbling in him. But whoever hates his brother walks in darkness and does not know where he is going, because the darkness has blinded his heart." What can you, creature of darkness, say to this? Why do you press those who stand in the light toward darkness, saying, "Hate along with me the man I hate unjustly; share in my madness; be murderers like me"? Then, if he says that whoever hates his brother walks in darkness and does not know where he is going, because the darkness of violence has blinded his eyes, what of someone who has killed his brother? What of one who has been a murderer? But the crime of murder seems nothing to you, since you are found to have shed the blood of so many servants of God. You dare to order the priests of God to do the things that please only your father the devil and you Arians, his sons.

The most holy apostle likewise exhorts us to keep to the path of righteousness so that we may be found worthy to be placed in everlasting rest; and you, most wise of men, drive us to come with you into eternal torments. "Little children, let no one deceive you. Whoever does righteousness is righteous; but whoever commits sin is of the devil, because the devil has sinned from the beginning. The Son of God was revealed for this purpose, to destroy the works of the devil." Since, then, the apostle says that sin is from the devil, and you compel us to commit capital crimes, what else can I call you but the devil's agent? I see you cherish his causes and look after his affairs so devotedly that you want all of us to be found on his side. For why else do you compel every worshipper of God to go over to him, unless because you have chosen to favour his party? You hear the blessed apostle say, "The Son of God was revealed for this reason, to destroy the works of the devil"; and you urge the worshippers of God to complete the devil's work. When you do these things, do you not appear to have set yourself up as the opponent of him who destroyed the devil's work? But it is no wonder that you have chosen to have what the only Son of God destroyed rebuilt through you, the devil's henchman, since you did not hesitate even to deny the very one who destroyed the devil's work. That is why shedding the blood of an innocent man means nothing to you: in denying the lover of the innocent and the defender of those who worship him, you have already gone over to the one to whom Judas Iscariot went over. If, then, you cannot deny that shedding the blood of a righteous man is the devil's work, it is perfectly clear that you have done the devil's work and urged us to do it. Further, John, most beloved of God, speaks so that brotherly love may be kept unbroken, saying: "By this the children of God and the children of the devil are made known. Everyone who is not righteous is not of God, nor is whoever does not love his brother. For this is the promise you have heard from the beginning, that we should love one another; not like Cain, who was of the evil one and killed his brother. And why did he kill him? Because his own works were evil and his brother's were righteous. Do not be surprised, brothers, if the world hates us. We know that we have passed from death to life, because we love the brothers; whoever does not love abides in death. Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer; and you know that no murderer has eternal life abiding in him." Since, therefore, everyone found hating his brother is called a son of the devil and a murderer, is likened to Cain the fratricide, and is marked out as abiding in death, why did you compel me to carry out this deed, which would have made me a fratricide like Cain and a son of the devil, and would have left me abiding in everlasting death? When you see that I have already passed from death to life, when God has already placed me among those he has deigned to call his sons, why did you want me to become Cain, darkness, and a son of the devil? How have I wronged you? In what have I stood against your salvation, that you should have wished me such harm? Why do we keep repeating these things, if not so that you may at last be able to understand, since you do not know what is good? For if you knew, you would never have committed so great a crime yourself, nor urged us to commit it. Meanwhile tell me, I pray, why do you persecute the bishop of God's house? For the apostle says that whoever hates his brother is a murderer. If you do not want to bear the name of murderer, why do you hate your brother? Prove that Athanasius deserves hatred; show what evil he has done, so that he may deserve to be hated by all of us too. You will certainly not produce any unjust deed of his that would make him hateful. Since this is so, it necessarily follows that you hate him because your work is evil and that of Athanasius is righteous. That is why you want to kill him: because he has not imitated you, wicked, criminal and sacrilegious as you are. That this is so is plain. For when the glorious apostle introduces the comparison between Cain and Abel, you seem to me to be Cain, and Athanasius Abel: "By this," he says, "the children of God and the children of the devil are made known. Everyone who is not righteous is not of God, nor is whoever does not love his brother. For this is the promise you have heard from the beginning, that we should love one another; not like Cain, who was of the evil one and killed his brother. And why did he kill him? Because his own works were evil and his brother's were righteous."

Nor should you doubt that your works are evil and Athanasius's righteous. For you are a murderer, a destroyer of God's religion, a denier of the only Son of God, an assailant of the apostolic faith, the founder of the Arian idolatry; Athanasius, on the other hand, so abides in the fear of God that, as far as can be seen, he is found to have committed nothing that could separate him from those most beloved of God. Since this is so, we urge you to love yourself in Athanasius. You remember what is written: "You shall love your neighbour as yourself," and "He who loves his neighbour has fulfilled the law." For just as you hate yourself in him, not knowing that it is evil to hate the righteous unjustly, so you will begin to love yourself in him if this malevolence of yours is turned into benevolence. Then you will be able to be rescued from the darkness in which, the blessed apostle says, you dwell. "Do not be surprised, brothers," he says, "if the world hates us. We know that we have passed from death to life, because we love the brothers. But whoever does not love remains in death. Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has life abiding in him." Do not dare any longer to say, "Condemn the innocent man," you who have no life abiding in you, you who have not yet passed from death to life. For if you had passed over, that is, if you had believed in the only Son of God as we do, you would not have chosen to be a murderer, lest you begin to go back again to death. So, set doubly without hope of life, you have seen fit to command priests to put an innocent man to death. But perhaps you may try to say: "I love those who love God, and I hate those who hate him." But this you cannot say of Athanasius, since it is rather plain that it is you who hate God, for you have both abandoned him and passed over to idolatry. And so, since you are persecuting no fault in the priest of God, but righteousness alone, the religion of God alone, it remains for you to see further how this blessed apostle John commanded us, whom you were urging to kill the innocent, to behave toward our fellow servants: "He laid down his life for us, and we ought to lay down our lives for the brothers." By the apostle I am commanded to lay down my life for my brother, and by you, the slave of Antichrist, I am ordered to kill my brother. And again he says: "Let us have confidence toward God, and whatever we ask we shall receive from him, because we keep his commandments; and let us do what is pleasing in his sight in the name of his Son Jesus Christ, and love one another, as he gave us commandment." But how shall I be heard by him in any supplication, if I do not keep his commandment? For he commanded me to love my brother, not to kill him. And further on: "Beloved, let us love one another, for love is from God." And again: "Whoever does not love his brother does not know God, for God is love. In this the love of God was made manifest among us, that God sent his only Son into the world, so that we might live through him. In this is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us and sent his Son as the expiation for our sins. Beloved, if God so loved us, we also ought to love one another." And again: "If anyone says that he loves God and hates his brother, he is a liar. For whoever does not love his brother cannot love God, whom he has not seen." And again: "This commandment we have from him, that whoever loves God should love his brother also." And again: "By this we know that we love the children of God, when we love God and do his commandments. For this is the love of God, and his commandments are not burdensome."

Look at these few passages out of many, and you will find into what darkness you have been dragging us, you man of darkness. "By this we know," he says, "that we love the children of God, because we love God and do his commandments. For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments." And you see fit to drive me to tear up these commandments and to set up others against them, which you have put forward at the devil's prompting. How can I be found to love God, if through you I am found to have become the adversary of his commandments? From such deeds, what do you seem to me to be but one of those tares destined for the fire? Of them the Lord says: "Just as the tares are gathered and burned with fire, so will it be at the end of the age. The Son of Man will send his angels, and they will gather out of his kingdom all causes of stumbling and those who do iniquity, and they will cast them into the furnace of fire; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth. Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father." You see that if, at your busy urging, heretic, I were to condemn an innocent man, I would be with you in Gehenna. For we could not attain the kingdom of God, in which we might shine like the sun, if we had either committed murder or violated the apostolic faith. Go on rejoicing that you live amid these evils; refuse to recognize the evils you are doing, and you will without doubt find yourself among those wicked ones whom the Lord marks out for the fire, saying: "The angels will go out and separate the wicked from the company of the righteous, and will cast them into the furnace of fire; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth." You see fit to think nothing of persecuting the servants of the only Son of God, you limb of the devil, who supposed that you could bring the whole holy church to stumbling. But look at what God promises you and all your fellows in sacrilege: "Whoever receives one such child in my name receives me; but whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be better for him to have a donkey's millstone hung around his neck and to be drowned in the depth of the sea. Woe to the world because of stumbling blocks! For stumbling blocks must come, but woe to that man through whom the stumbling block comes. If your hand or your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it away from you." And further on: "See that you do not despise one of these little ones; for I tell you that their angels in heaven always see the face of my Father who is in heaven." So then, since you not only despise those who believe in his divine majesty but even kill them, what wages will he pay you, he whom you deny? He said it would be better for you to have a donkey's millstone hung around your neck and be hurled into the depth of the sea than to bring one of those who believe in him to stumble, or to despise one of those who are to possess the kingdom of heaven. What will he pay you, who have deserved to be cut off from the members of his holy church for this reason: that you are the one through whom the devil has sent stumbling blocks among the people of God in our days? Although you have stirred up stumbling blocks, you have deceived only those who did not know that you had already withered, like a stream cut off from its spring, like a branch broken from a tree. But we, who know that you are set outside the church, who see in you the enemy of the only Son of God, know that you are dead, and we see your efforts, with God's help, beneath our feet. For we know that the dead cannot rule over the living. But why do you say that you live in Christ? How can you prove it, when you deny him? For none can live but those who confess him to be true God, the true Son of God. How are you alive, when you persecute us precisely because we confess that we are his servants?

Or do you persecute us for some other reason? Have you perhaps found that we have wronged you, and is that why you are so hostile toward us? We do not recall having sinned against you. For how could it be proved that we sinned against you, when we are urging you to come from death to life? And yet, if you feel that we have wronged you, hear what the Lord has commanded you to do toward us, saying: "If your brother sins against you, go and reprove him between you and him alone; if he listens to you, you have gained your brother. But if he does not listen to you, take one or two more along with you, so that every word may be established by the mouth of two or three witnesses. If he does not listen to them, tell it to the church; and if he does not listen to the church, let him be to you as a Gentile and a tax collector." You have not done what the Lord commanded to be done. Not only did you fail to admonish us privately, between yourself and us, so that in our presence you might prove Athanasius, one of us, guilty; you even forced him to be condemned unheard by us, his fellow priests, when you took away his hearing. How then can you justly accuse us of having wronged you, when you have fulfilled none of these commandments of the Lord? Why do you persecute us so fiercely, when it is rather you who are guilty of transgression, since you did not act toward us at all as the only Son of God commanded you, but did everything as it pleased our enemy the devil? For his is counsel of this kind, and his is such a will: that a man be condemned unheard, that he be killed in his absence, that the blood of the innocent be shed. Since, I say, you did not handle the matter in the way the Lord commanded you, yet you dared to bring it before the blessed church, you dared to say: "Athanasius has sinned, and communion with him ought to be condemned by all." But what will you try to say? That he has sinned against God? Yet look, it cannot be found that he sinned against God, since neither you nor your fellows in sacrilege, the sons of the harlot, the Arian heresy, can be admitted as witnesses against a catholic bishop. For the Lord was speaking of three catholic witnesses, servants of his majesty, so that the blessed church might believe them, not profane men born of adultery from a harlot. Otherwise, if we do not understand this precept of the Lord in this way, the worshippers of Saturn and of all the idols could also be admitted as witnesses against God's household, and so could your fellow blasphemers the Jews, forsaken by God and set without light, as you are. For if you heretics, of every sect whatever, are to be admitted as witnesses against Christians, then pagans and Jews must be admitted too, since whether Jews or pagans or you heretics, placed outside the Lord's church you are without God, like all those long ago who were not in the ark of most holy Noah. For as they, being outside the ark, could not be saved, so neither can you; you will perish in the same way, unless you believe in the only Son of God and abide with us in his holy church. If, then, neither you nor your fellow blasphemers can be witnesses, how did you, most witless king, have a man of perfect innocence condemned, and by his own fellow priests at that? I add this: that you had already accused him of being a murderer at Serdica, in the synod of catholics, and your iniquity was utterly unable to prove it. I add that you yourself sent letters to the church of the Alexandrians affirming that he was a just man and a catholic bishop. Finally, even if he had sinned, Athanasius ought to have been removed by the people entrusted to him, and in such a way that that people might ask for another worthy man from its own body to be made its bishop; he was not to be hunted down with the sword by you, the emperor. But in place of an innocent man against whom you established nothing true, in place of a catholic, you sent your fellow in sacrilege, George; and on those unwilling to be stained by his sacrilege you inflicted such insults and such punishments that you proscribed very many, banished them into exile and to the mines, and even killed a great many; and to this day you do not cease to do to those who refuse to accept your blasphemy, which is also George's, things that even enraged enemies, the most savage barbarians, would scarcely do. How then do you think you can be taken for a Christian, when you are seen to be fiercer than the most savage wild beasts and more monstrous than any brute? You dared to say that Athanasius should be struck down, not seeing that you Arians were punished back then, and indeed by the power of God, when you planned to bring idolatry into the Lord's church.

But perhaps you may still say: "Athanasius has wronged me." To pass over the fact that in this too you are lying, did you not know what is written, what the Lord commanded you to do toward those who wrong you, that you should have pursued him with the sword like this? "Then Peter came up to him and said to him: 'Lord, if my brother sins against me, how often shall I forgive him? As many as seven times?' He said to him: 'I do not say to you seven times, but seventy times seven.'" Or are you ashamed to hear Athanasius called your brother? If you profess yourself a Christian, you ought to call all Christians brothers, and not only Athanasius but also those you see begging for alms. For all of us who are set in the Lord's church are one to him, with whom there is no respect of persons. And yet you would do well not to wish him called your brother; for since you are a son of pestilence and he is one of the sons of light, since you are the slave of our enemy and he is a servant of God, it would be most unjust for you, the forerunner of Antichrist, to be called the brother of a man of God. If you saw that he had wronged you in anything, you ought to have forgiven him at once, so that God might forgive you your own crimes. But now, since you could not forgive because of your obstinacy and malevolence, hear, you who have made void the Lord's precept, what may be paid back to you: "Then Peter came up to him and said: 'Lord, if my brother sins against me, how often shall I forgive him? As many as seven times?' He said to him: 'I do not say to you seven times, but seventy times seven. Therefore the kingdom of heaven has been likened to a king who wished to settle accounts with his servants. When he began to settle accounts, one was brought to him who owed ten thousand talents.
