And since he had nothing with which to pay, his lord ordered him to be sold, with his wife and children and all that he had, and the debt to be repaid. So that servant fell down and begged him, saying: "Have patience with me, and I will repay you everything." And the lord of that servant took pity on him, released him, and forgave him the debt. But that servant went out and found one of his fellow servants who owed him a hundred denarii, and seizing him he began to choke him, saying: "Pay what you owe." And that servant fell down and begged him, saying: "Have patience with me, and I will repay you." But he refused, and went and threw him into prison until he should pay the debt. When his fellow servants saw what had happened, they were greatly distressed, and they went and told their lord all that had taken place. Then his lord summoned him and said to him: "You wicked servant, I forgave you all that debt because you begged me; should not you also have had pity on your fellow servant, as I had pity on you?" And in anger his lord handed him over to the torturers until he should pay the whole debt. So also my Father who is in heaven will do to you, if each of you does not forgive his brother from your hearts.'" What do you answer to this, you whose mind's eyes could not see at all what the Lord commanded to be done? What do you make of the fact that Athanasius has wronged neither you nor God, but is suffering persecution because he holds the apostolic faith, because he refuses to become a sacrilegist, as you are? You have resolved to kill the preacher of truth, desiring to set yourself in the same rank as those whom the Lord marks out in the gospel as the killers of the prophets, and whom he reveals as about to stretch out impious hands even against himself, saying: "There was a householder who planted a vineyard, put a hedge around it, dug a winepress in it, built a tower, leased it to tenants, and went abroad. When the time of the fruit drew near, he sent his servants to the tenants to receive his fruit; and the tenants seized his servants, beat one, stoned another, and killed another. Again he sent more servants to them, and they did the same to them. Last of all he sent them his only son, saying: 'They will respect my son.' But when the tenants saw the son, they said among themselves: 'This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and we shall have his inheritance.' And they seized him, killed him, and threw him out of the vineyard. When, therefore, the lord of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those tenants?" They said to him: "He will put those wicked men to a wretched death and lease the vineyard to other tenants, who will give him the fruit in their seasons."

Since you greatly desire to be one of these, you were also urging us to become partners in your crimes. For your counsels are no different from the wicked counsels of those who are found to have killed the prophets, and who in the end stretched out impious hands against the only Son of God. This is all the more so because you are even reducing to nothing the sufferings of those blessed men who were sent to the tenants, by asserting that they were killed for the sake of one of whom there was a time when he was not, although the sacred scriptures proclaim that the only Son of God has always reigned and reigns with the Father. The Lord's writings reveal that the Father and his only Son have one deity; and you say that he for whom the glorious prophets were killed was made out of nothing. For if what you say is true, it is evident that the blessed prophets were killed for a creature. And then what becomes of the fact that the Lord is angry with great indignation at those who serve the creature rather than the Creator? If the blessed prophets were killed for a creature, how can God hold them most dear? How is it that the Jews, because they did not believe their words, are today God's enemies? Why are the Jews God's enemies? Why are they found set outside the Lord's vineyard? Is it not because they were the killers of the prophets, because the prophets preached the eternal God, the Son of the eternal God, and those fellow blasphemers of yours not only did not believe their prophecy but even killed them? For whom do you think the Jews persecuted in the prophets but the only Son of God, as they also did in the apostles and martyrs? Learn from yourself, at least, that what I say is true, since you too persecute the true Son of God both in Athanasius and in us. This being so, you had resolved that we should be joined to the killers of the prophets, the shedders of the blood of the righteous, your fellows in sacrilege, that is, the Jews, plainly because you are their imitator. For you said "Condemn Athanasius" and ordered us to accept the faith of Arius as well for no other reason than that we might be equal to the Jews, both in shedding the blood of the righteous and in denying the only Son of God; and you are already their partner in everything. For if they killed the prophets, those who spoke of the coming of the only Son of God, you too kill those who believe as the prophets believed. But how long shall I go on about these things with an unbeliever, when I set out to show you that you are one of those to whom the Lord says: "Therefore I tell you that the kingdom of God will be taken away from you and given to a nation producing its fruit"? For you do not belong to that nation which is found to produce the fruits of righteousness; and so you are declared to be one of those who, as you hear, were driven from God's kingdom because of the slaughter of the righteous and their own unbelief. Take note that by doing these things you are among those whose wickedness the Lord lays bare, saying: "The kingdom of heaven is like a king who gave a wedding feast for his son and sent his servants to call those invited to the wedding," and further on: "and they would not come. Again he sent servants, saying: 'Tell those who are invited: See, I have prepared my dinner; my bulls and fatted cattle have been slaughtered, and everything is ready; come to the wedding.' But they paid no attention and went off, some to their farms, others to their business; and the rest seized his servants, treated them shamefully, and killed them. When the king heard of it, he was angry, and he sent his army, destroyed those murderers, and burned their cities. Then he said to his servants: 'The wedding is ready, but those who were invited were not worthy. Go therefore to the crossroads, and invite to the wedding whomever you find.' And the servants went out into the roads and gathered all whom they found, both bad and good, and the wedding hall was filled with guests. But when the king came in to look at the guests, he saw there a man not clothed in a wedding garment, and he said to him: 'Friend, how did you come in here without a wedding garment?' And he was speechless. Then the king said to the attendants: 'Take him by the feet and hands and throw him into the outer darkness; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.'" Since, then, you are without the wedding garment, Constantius, you will be for ever, unless you are converted, like the man to whom it is said: "Friend, how did you come in here without a wedding garment?" And so you will go into the outer darkness.

Do not doubt that you will come into the outer darkness, since you have already been turned wholly into darkness. For those who shed the blood of the righteous prophets and denied the only Son of God are called both darkness and sons of the devil. Since you too are doing these things, you will surely remain a son both of darkness and of the devil, unless you look to your own good. "How," you say, "can I look to my own good?" By ceasing to persecute us and by accepting the apostolic faith. Unless you do this, you will always be, as you are now, among those to whom it is said: "Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, who tithe mint and dill and cumin, and have neglected the weightier matters of the law: judgment, mercy and faith. These you ought to have done, without leaving the others undone. Blind guides, straining out a gnat and swallowing a camel!" If you do not deserve to hear these words along with them, where is the just judgment that comes from you, who strive to kill a righteous man because he preaches the apostolic faith? Where is the just judgment, when you persecute with all the forces of your empire those you see unwilling either to condemn a man unheard or to abandon the catholic faith, and you love those you know to have joined you in shedding innocent blood and rejecting the faith of the gospel? What mercy is there with you, established in you, the mercy that the holy law commanded us to show? Plainly the kind that tortures, proscribes, deports, casts into prison, drives into exile and sends to the mines; the kind that kills by hunger, thirst, beatings and nakedness; and, finally, the kind that punishes with the sword. This, Constantius, is your mercy, which comes not from the law of God but from the presumption of the devil. "Judgment and mercy and faith," he says: "these you ought to have done, without leaving the others undone." Where is your faith? You condemned the faith held by the most blessed Abraham, Isaac and Jacob and by all the prophets, apostles and martyrs, and decreed that all who worship God must accept the faith that the devil vomited up against this catholic faith through your teacher Arius. From all this you are understood to be one of those who are seen to hear: "Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, who tithe mint and dill and cumin, and have neglected the weightier matters of the law: judgment, mercy and faith. These you ought to have done, without leaving the others undone. Blind guides, straining out a gnat and swallowing a camel!" Or will you deny that you strain out the gnat and swallow the camel? You give alms not only when asked but sometimes even of your own accord, and yet, as has often been said, you proscribe those who confess that they are Christians, deport them, torture them, and in the end kill them. So you must recognize that you are among those to whom it is said: "Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for you are like whitewashed tombs, which outwardly look beautiful to men, but inside are full of dead men's bones and all filth. So you too outwardly look righteous to men, but inside you are full of hypocrisy and iniquity." You are one of those murderers to whom it is said: "Serpents, brood of vipers, how will you escape the judgment of Gehenna? Therefore, behold, I send you prophets and wise men and scribes, and some of them you will kill and crucify, and persecute from city to city, so that upon you may come all the righteous blood shed on the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah son of Barachiah, whom you killed between the temple and the altar. Amen, I say to you, all these things will come upon this generation."

Your deeds prove that you belong to that brood of vipers. For you are found to be one of those to whom these words were spoken because they would commit these deeds. Or if you deny that you are one of those who hear from the Lord's mouth, "Serpents, brood of vipers," then prove that it was not you but the Jews who dispatched soldiers to Alexandria, that it was soldiers of the Jews who besieged the doors of God's house, and that Syrianus was the commander of soldiers of the Jews. Prove that it was the Jews who entered the church with weapons and killed a number of people. If you cannot prove it, since it is established that you sent them to attack the religion of God, we are entirely right to say that you are one of those to whom it was said: "Serpents, brood of vipers, how will you escape the judgment of Gehenna?" Without doubt you will not escape the judgment of Gehenna, but you will burn there forever with your fellow serpents, unless you look out for yourself. "Then," he says, "they will hand you over to tribulation and kill you, and you will be hated by all nations for my name's sake. And then many will fall away and betray one another and hate one another. And many false prophets will arise and lead many astray. And because iniquity will abound, the love of many will grow cold." If your sacrilegious mind does not know that I suffer persecution from you for the sake of the only Son of God, then you may not belong to that brood, and may not fall under the sentence of those to whom it is said: "Serpents, brood of vipers, how will you escape the judgment of Gehenna? Therefore, behold, I send you prophets and wise men and scribes, and some of them you will kill and crucify, and persecute from city to city." Since you are doing these very things today, you will not dare deny that you are the offspring of the viper. For you have killed a great many Christians in many places, and you hold others in chains in prisons and workhouses. From this too you can see that you are one of those to whom it is said, "Serpents, brood of vipers," and further on, "Behold, I send you prophets and wise men and scribes, and some of them you will kill." For you do not see fit to curse those whose love has grown cold, whom you see to have departed from the apostolic faith through your abounding iniquity. Instead you curse those you see remaining in that state of faith in which the blessed prophets, apostles and martyrs remained, and so were found worthy to gain God's eternal friendship. At Alexandria you do not curse the presbyters Achetas and Didymas, who are known to have turned from Christians into Arians; you curse those you know still stand with us. If that is not so, why do you not curse Didymas and Achetas now, whom you used to curse before? It can only be that you then held them accursed because they were still Christians, while now they are very dear to you because they have become blasphemers, apostates like you. But now, after so many proofs have been laid before you that you are one of those to whom it is said, "Serpents, brood of vipers, how will you escape the judgment of Gehenna?", we trust that you will make an effort to heal the grievous wounds the devil has inflicted on you, for you are both a murderer and a sacrilegious man. If you refuse to be freed from these crimes, your blood will be required of you, and we shall stand before God clean of your blood, since we have revealed the truth to you in every way. And not only your own blood will be required of you, but also the blood of those whom you have either led to embrace heresy or enticed into murdering an innocent man.

But you may say: "I thought that the faith of those you call Arians was the catholic faith." Suppose you wavered in the matter of faith; suppose you did not know that those who say they believe in a creature, who say that God has no true Son, are heretics. Were you also ignorant of this, that it is not just to persecute an innocent man with the sword? Had you forgotten that the Lord said to blessed Peter, "Put your sword back in its place; for all who take the sword will perish by the sword"? What then will you do, Constantius, you who have killed so great a multitude of the servants of Christ, the only Son of God? For you see that he whom you persecute in us says that all who take the sword will perish by the sword. What will you receive? Unless you obtain pardon for your crimes by believing in him whom you deny, you will deserve to be struck by the sword of God as many times as you have struck those devoted to his mercy. Who are you, a mere man, to say that God's priests must be compelled to strike down an absent man, to punish one who has not been heard, to shed innocent blood? Why did you refuse to let our fellow bishop Athanasius be heard by us? Why did you want us to murder the man of God secretly, like brigands? It can only be because you are one of those in reproach of whom these words were spoken: "No one has ascended into heaven except the one who descended from heaven, the Son of Man who is in heaven. And just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so the Son of Man must be lifted up, so that everyone who believes in him may have eternal life. For God so loved the world that he gave his only Son, so that everyone who believes in him may not perish but have eternal life. For God did not send his Son into the world to judge the world, but so that the world might be saved through him. Whoever believes in him is not judged; but whoever does not believe in him is already judged, because he has not believed in the name of the only Son of God. And this is the judgment: that the light has come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, for their deeds were evil. Everyone who does evil hates the light and does not come to the light, so that his deeds may not be exposed. But whoever does the truth comes to the light, so that his deeds may be shown to have been done in God." If you recognized yourself as a servant of the only Son of God, you would certainly never deny his majesty, and never order his servants to be murdered, now in secret, now in public. But because you are a lover of darkness, indeed darkness itself, since your works are evil, you refused to let the charge you had brought be fully examined by God's priests. Why did you refuse? Only because you feared that your serpent's work would be made public. "While we are in the body," says the apostle, "we are away from the Lord; for we walk by faith, not by sight. We are bold, and of good will we would rather be away from the body and present with the Lord; and we strive, whether absent or present, to please him. For we must all be made manifest before the judgment seat of Christ, so that each may receive what is due for what he did in the body, whether good or evil." And you, Constantius the heretic, say: "Christians, condemn a Christian!" Why do you say this? Only because you have judged it best to shed the blood of the righteous, to forsake God, and to take up idolatry.

But again I beg you, most pious emperor, since you both deny the only Son of God and persecute those who believe in him, to consider whether you are not found to be the equal of those whose wickedness is described in the Acts of the Apostles: "When a great dissension arose among them, the tribune, fearing that Paul would be torn to pieces by them, ordered the soldiers to go down, snatch him from among them and bring him into the barracks. The following night the Lord stood by him and said: 'Be steadfast; for as you have testified about me in Jerusalem, so you must testify in Rome as well.' When day came, some of the Jews gathered and bound themselves by an oath, saying that they would neither eat nor drink until they had killed Paul. There were about forty who had formed this conspiracy, and they went to the chief priests and told them: 'We have bound ourselves by a solemn vow to taste nothing at all until we have killed Paul. Now, therefore, you must convene the council and give notice to the tribune to bring him down to you, as though you meant to examine his case more carefully; and we are ready to kill him before he comes near.'" Did you not hunt Athanasius, the priest of God, in just this way? Did you not pretend to be doing one thing while planning to accomplish another? Can you then deny that you too are driven by the same hostile spirit that drove the Jews and drives them still? Had you not been stirred up by that spirit against us who serve God, you would surely never have ordered an absent man, and an innocent one at that, to be condemned. I repeat these things so often as though even you, in the moments when the goads of your fury leave you in peace, did not realize how completely you have strayed from the rule of justice. You could not even see in the Acts of the Apostles that when the Jews demanded that the blessed Paul be put to death, Festus, a pagan governor, refused to give his assent to the assembly of the Jews, and instead promised to hear both them and Paul together, face to face. The pagan kept the law of equity; you destroyed it. Or is it equity to condemn a man unheard, to kill a man in his absence, and to deny a hearing to a righteous man, a man for whom all God's people bear witness that he was falsely accused by you and yours, a Christian accused by you Arians? So, as I had begun to say, hear what Festus did in the case between the Jews and the blessed Paul: "When Festus had come into the province as governor, he went up to Jerusalem [?] laying an ambush to kill him on the way. Festus answered that Paul was being kept at Caesarea, and that he himself would be leaving shortly. 'So let those of you who are able go down, and if there is any wrong in the man, let them accuse him.' After staying among them no more than eight or ten days, he went down to Caesarea, and the next day he took his seat on the tribunal and ordered Paul to be brought in. When he had been brought, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around him, bringing many serious charges which they could not prove, while Paul argued in his defence that he had committed no offence against the law of the Jews, or against the temple, or against Caesar." A heathen held to the path of equity between the blessed Paul and the Jews, your fellow murderers; and you, eager to obey the desires of your evil designs, decided that equity and justice must be driven from our minds.

But how could we have done what you were forcing us to do against justice, when we remembered that it is written: "Do not judge by appearances, but judge with just judgment"? When you said, "Condemn him unheard," why did you not remember that Nicodemus said: "Does our law judge a man without first hearing from him and learning what he has done?" Why did you refuse to let the man you declared worthy of death be heard, unless it was because the charges you had brought were false? The Lord says to the Jews: "Whoever speaks a lie speaks from his own, for he is a liar, and so is his father." And you, though you have plainly shown yourself a liar, imagine that you are not the son of the liar? Do you dare, son of the liar, to resist — a deceiver against the truthful, a sacrilegious man against the Lord's priests? You dare this, when we see that you are that robber and thief whom the Lord foretold, saying: "Amen, amen, I say to you, whoever does not enter the sheepfold by the door but climbs in another way is a thief and a robber." You did indeed stretch out your hands to seize Christ's sheep for the Antichrist; but once you were recognized as a thief and a robber, you were shunned and rejected. Why did God's sheep not follow you, or your fellow in sacrilege, George? Why do they follow the man whose position as bishop of the Alexandrians grieves you so bitterly? It can only be because God appointed him their bishop, while the devil sent you and George in among them as robbers and thieves to slaughter them. "He who enters by the door," he says, "is the shepherd of the sheep. The doorkeeper opens to him, and the sheep hear his voice; he calls his own sheep by name and leads them out, and when he has brought out all his own, he goes before them, and the sheep follow him, because they know his voice. A stranger they will not follow, but will flee from him, because they do not know his voice." Since, then, you have not entered the church by the door, you are plainly seen to be a robber and a thief. For you do not know the Son of God, and so cannot claim to have entered by the door. He called them thieves and robbers because they did not believe in his divine mercy then, nor would they believe afterwards, and they would try to teach his sheep otherwise. Since you are spreading an insane doctrine on this very point, because you have not believed in him, your blasphemies prove beyond all doubt that you are that robber and thief who was already foretold then. The rest of the saying proves that this is so: "Jesus said to them: Amen, amen, I say to you, I am the door of the sheep. All who came before me are thieves and robbers, but the sheep did not listen to them. I am the door; if anyone enters through me, he will be saved, and will go in and find pasture. The thief comes only to steal." You thief, then, who are found to have entered God's sheepfold for the very purpose of stealing and killing, how can you still say, "Athanasius ought not to be bishop of the Alexandrians, but George," when you see that you and George and all your fellows in sacrilege are nothing but thieves and robbers? God willed his servants to be shepherds over the flock, so that they would recognize you and yours as robbers and thieves and drive you out.

But you decided that we, whom God had ordained, should be driven out and that you and yours should preside over the Lord's flock, so that you could ravage God's flock freely. Since you are such a man, we cannot be surprised that you said a worshipper of God should be punished in his absence. For you could not keep in mind that the Lord said: "If you love me, keep my commandments. And I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Advocate, to be with you forever, the Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive, because it neither sees him nor knows him; you know him, because he abides with you and is in you." But tell me, I beg you, how could the Holy Spirit, the Paraclete, dwell in us if we had done your will, or the will of your father? Further on he says: "Whoever hears my commandments and keeps them is the one who hears me. And whoever loves me will be loved by my Father, and I will love him and show myself to him. Judas, not Iscariot, said to him: 'Lord, how is it that you will show yourself to us and not to this world?' Jesus answered him: 'If anyone loves me, he will keep my word, and my Father will love him, and we will come to him and make our dwelling with him. Whoever does not love me does not keep my words.'" From these sayings of the Lord one can gauge how great an enemy of ours you have shown yourself to be: "Whoever hears my commandments and keeps them is the one who loves me." How could we have shown that we loved him if, like you, we trampled on his commandments? For you trample on the Lord's commandments: what he decreed must be kept, you not only order not to be kept, but you even command that he himself be denied. Or how could his Father love me for keeping his Son's commandments, if I condemned an innocent man? The Son of God says: "If anyone loves me, he will keep my word, and my Father will love him, and we will come to him and make our dwelling with him"; and you, apostate, fodder for the fire, say: "Condemn the innocent man!" How would we have been found to love the Son of God if, against his commandments, we had murdered a righteous man? How could the Father have loved us, and the Father and the Son have come and deigned to dwell in us, if we had torn up the Lord's commandments and kept the orders of a sacrilegious man like you? Consider, Constantius, from what glory that envious devil, who loves your will, tried through you, his client, to drive us. He would have succeeded had the Lord's goodness not come to our help, so that we no longer regarded you as a man whom God made in his image and likeness, but as the filth of all the sewers, and trampled on your sacrilegious commands. For who, unless he were more wretched than you Arians, would not wish to be loved by the only Son of God? Who would not wish to be loved by his Father? Who would refuse to be a temple of the Father and of his only Son? These things cannot be attained by one who, like you, has been both a murderer and sacrilegious; yet even you can attain them, if you turn and truly repent. The Lord says further: "This is my commandment, that you love one another as I have loved you. No one has greater love than this, to lay down his life for his friends. You are my friends if you do what I command you. I no longer call you servants, but friends"; and again: "You did not choose me, but I chose you and appointed you to go and bear fruit, and that your fruit should remain, so that whatever you ask the Father in my name he may give you,"

How could we be friends of the only Son of God if, against the prohibition of his goodness, we condemned an absent man and killed an innocent one? How could our fruit grow and increase? How would we receive from the Father whatever we asked in his name if, as you were forcing us to do, we not only punished his worshipper but also denied him? Had you not found what the blessed Apostle wrote to Titus, a man dedicated to God, about the blameless office of a bishop, and what it is fitting for him to offer to God, that you should want us to become murderers? "This is why I left you in Crete, that you might set right what was lacking and appoint elders in every city, as I directed you: if anyone is blameless, the husband of one wife, having believing children who are not open to the charge of debauchery or insubordinate. For a bishop must be blameless, as God's steward, not arrogant, not quick-tempered, not given to drink, not violent, not greedy for shameful gain, but hospitable, kind, sober, just, holy, self-controlled, holding fast to the faithful word that accords with the teaching, so that he may be able to exhort in sound doctrine and to refute those who contradict it. For there are many who are insubordinate, empty talkers and deceivers, especially those of the circumcision, who must be refuted, since they overturn whole households, teaching what they ought not for the sake of shameful gain." Since, then, he wanted a bishop to be someone who lived by holding to this path of justice, by what authority have you deigned to issue new commands that shut out the commands of the blessed Apostle? Commands, that is, which are known to have sprung from the will of the devil. The Apostle wants me not to be quick-tempered, not violent, and you want me to become a murderer. From this it can be gathered that the Holy Spirit spoke through the mouth of the blessed Apostle, but an evil spirit through the mouth of you Arians. You see, meanwhile, that the Apostle commanded that you who resist the truth should be [?] through the intervention of a bishop, so that your blasphemy might be punished through sound doctrine. I have not cited the blessed Apostle's saying that a bishop must be blameless in order to deny that I am a sinner, since I know my own conscience, and I hear that just man Job saying: "For who is clean from filth? No one, even if his life on earth is but a single day"; I also note the blessed John saying: "If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us." So I have not cited the Apostle's precept in order to proclaim myself spotless, when I remember that I am a sinner, but so that you might see how evil is the thing you have commanded to be done. "Likewise," he says, "urge the young men to be sober in all things, showing yourself in everything a model of good works, in teaching, in integrity, in dignity, in sound and blameless speech, so that the opponent may be put to shame, having nothing evil to say about us."

How would I have offered myself to others as a model of good works if I had shed the blood of a servant of God? How would the peoples of God have recognized me as preaching the sound doctrine the apostles handed down if I had embraced your heresy, or if, in short, I had communicated, even in hypocrisy, with your henchmen, the Arian false bishops? How could my speech be put forth sound and blameless if I had abandoned the evangelical and apostolic faith and embraced your blasphemy? How could the opponent have been put to shame? How could he have nothing evil to say about me, when, had I decided to give in to you, he would have caught me made both a murderer and a sacrilegious man? Again, when he was admonishing slaves that they ought to be subject to their masters, he says: "For the grace of God our Savior has shone upon all people, correcting us, so that, renouncing ungodliness and worldly desires, we may live soberly, devoutly and justly in this age, awaiting the blessed hope, the coming of the glory of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ, who gave himself for us to set us free from all iniquity and to cleanse for himself a people of his own, zealous for good works." Since he has commanded us to walk in these good works, what possessed you to strive to commit murder? For how could we have been seen as renouncing ungodliness and living devoutly and justly if we had shed innocent blood with you? Moreover, since he says that the Lord gave himself up for our sins precisely in order to snatch us from the works of Satan and to establish us for this, that we should be zealous for good works, if we too had carried out this work of yours with you, in what portion would we be, except the one where Cain is? "For the grace of God our Savior," he says, "has shone upon all people, correcting us, so that, renouncing ungodliness and worldly desires, we may live soberly, justly and devoutly in this age." And you, Emperor Constantius, deign to say: let us be ungodly, wicked, lost, malicious, iniquitous, unjust. Where shall I find this blessed hope which the blessed Apostle teaches me I must await, if I not only kill the servants of him who has power to bestow all blessedness, but also deny him himself? For you do both, Constantius: you persecute and kill his servants, and, deserting him, you have decided to make yourself a slave to idols. Why do you do these things, except because the grace of God our Savior has not shone upon you? For if it had shone upon you, you would remember the precepts of the Apostle when he says: "See, then, that you walk carefully, not as unwise but as wise, redeeming the time, because the days are evil. Therefore do not be foolish, but understand what the will of the Lord is." If it is the Lord's will to kill an innocent man and to abandon the evangelical faith, then not only this passage but the whole body of the blessed Apostle's letters could lend support to your decrees; but if no part of the sacred Scriptures favors your decrees, it is clearer than daylight that you live under the power of darkness. Hence it has come about that you have drawn nothing from the sacred springs of the Scriptures that could have kept you away from such great dangers. For if the power of darkness had not brought you under its sway, you would surely remember what the Philippians hear: "Be fellow imitators of me, brothers, and observe those who walk according to the model you have in us. For many walk, of whom I often told you, and now tell you even with tears, as enemies of the cross of Christ; their end is destruction, their god is their belly, and their glory is in their shame; they have their minds on earthly things."

I would like you to tell me, most prudent Emperor, in what respects we ought to become fellow imitators of the Apostle. Teach us, apostate: was the Apostle a murderer, a blasphemer, a destroyer of the evangelical faith, a sacrilegious man? For he does admit to having done all these things before he believed in the only Son of God. But you, who today do the things he did before he came to know the only Son of God, on what ground did you dare to order us, the Lord's priests, to condemn an innocent man, and to embrace your heresy and spit out the apostolic faith? On what ground did you command these things to be done, which are set forth against the model of the Apostle, except because you are one of the enemies of the cross of Christ, one of those of you who were marked out even then by the mouth of the holy Apostle? Should we listen to you and your people, whose end the Apostle says is destruction? To those henchmen of yours who, abandoning the model of discipline handed down and the rule of faith from the apostles, have given themselves over to you for the sake of shameful gain; those who have made more of the plenty of your table than of what the Lord promises his own; those who have chosen to be your table companions rather than those of the patriarchs, prophets, apostles and martyrs, to whom it is said most rightly: "Your god is your belly"? "Test everything," says the Apostle, "hold fast what is good, keep yourselves from every form of evil"; and because we have seen the accursed work of you Arians and have shunned it, we suffer hatred. But how fine and how delightful it is to be hated by you and loved by God! You have driven us from the charge entrusted to us, thinking you could destroy what God has built. Writing to the Ephesians, he says: "But to each one of us grace was given according to the measure of Christ's favor. Therefore it says: 'Ascending on high he led captivity captive; he gave gifts to men.' Now what does 'he ascended' mean, except that he also descended into the lower parts of the earth? He who descended is the same one who also ascended above all the heavens, that he might fill all things. And he gave some as apostles, some as prophets, some as evangelists, some as pastors and teachers, for the perfecting of the saints, for the work of ministry, for the building up of the body of Christ, until we all attain to the unity of the faith and the knowledge of God, to a perfect man, to the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ, so that we may no longer be little children, tossed about and carried around by every wind of doctrine, by the wickedness of men, by craftiness in the contrivances of error. But doing the truth in love, let us grow up in every way into him who is the head, Christ, from whom the whole body, joined and knit together through every supporting joint, according to the measure of each part, makes the body grow so that it builds itself up in love."

Since you read that this is so, why did you dare to remove the shepherds whom God willed to be over his flock? Why? Except so that the shepherds set by God over the Lord's flock might be carried about with you by every wind of doctrine. Was it not so that those coming to the faith might be led like little children by every wind of doctrine? So that, through the craftiness of you most wicked men, they might withdraw from the apostolic and evangelical faith to the contrivances of the devil, your prince? You have taken away the bishops from the peoples over whom we preside by God's favor, precisely so that you might teach a doctrine that is not apostolic but heretical. Woe to you, wretched man, through whom Satan does these things! You found, wise man that you are, a fitting color for your deceit, a way to [?] God's sheep to your father, who, so that you might linger in these evils, has already pierced your heart with the same darts with which he wounded the minds of Eve and Adam, namely in order to fix you firmly in this depravity. You found, I say, wise man that you are, a fitting color for your deceit, a way to lay waste the Lord's flock, saying: "Athanasius has sinned, and therefore whoever destroys him along with me will be a bishop; whoever decides to disregard this will not be." And those who condemned Athanasius were joined to the false bishops of your Arian doctrine. If any did this out of fear of your wrath, they incurred, through you, a murderer and sacrilegious man, a threefold crime: they condemned an innocent man, they, though Catholics, communicated with heretics, and they allowed you wolves to enter God's flock. Yet the Apostle says that shepherds were given precisely so that every doctrine of demons, which is put forth through you heretics and all the adversaries of the Church, might be shut out, and so that God's servants, running in the truth, might remain unmoved until they came to the highest perfection. And you, darkness that you are, have deigned to remove the shepherds appointed by God's judgment, so that you, a wolf, might turn them all into prey for the devil, your lover. "So that we may no longer be little children," he says, "tossed about and carried around by every wind of doctrine, by the wickedness of men, by craftiness in the contrivances of error. But doing the truth in love, let us grow up in every way into him who is the head, Christ." How could we grow up into him if we had followed you, darkness, since you deny that he is true God, since you say that he was not born of the substance of the Father, but maintain that he was made from nothing? How could we have grown up into him, we who would not be walking in the truth, from the moment we had followed you, an apostate? Then, since he says, "Doing the truth, let us grow in love," and since it is plain that Athanasius, a priest of God, has been attacked with false charges by you and your people, if we had done what you command, how could we have been seen running either in truth or in love, we who would have extinguished the love we hold with our fellow bishop Athanasius? And because we would have [?] a false charge, and would ourselves have joined you, the deceiver, in the death of an innocent man, we would deserve to be struck down together with you by God's indignation. Is this, then, Constantius, how the house of God is built: by deceit, by shedding the blood of the innocent, by blasphemous preaching? Woe to you, who live only so that the devil may do all these evils through you!

You say to me: "Punish an innocent man, abandon the Catholic faith and take up the poisons of my heresy"; and there is the Apostle saying: "This, then, I say and testify in the Lord, that you no longer walk as the Gentiles walk, in the futility of their mind, darkened in understanding, alienated from the life of God through the ignorance that is in them, because of the blindness of their heart." Which of you two should I obey? You or the Apostle? You, a sacrilegious apostate, or him who is found to have already shed his blood for the only Son of God? Which of you should I follow? You, a temple of demons, or him, a temple of God? You, who by your works declare yourself either a Jew or a pagan, or him who has already obtained the heavenly kingdom through this faith which you curse? For if you do not show by your works that you are a pagan, you can argue that these things are said against you unjustly. First, since you deny the Son of God, you are to us a pagan or a Jew; second, when you proscribe, deport and torture the innocent, burden them with false charges and kill them, you cannot be found to be a Christian, one recognized by his way of life as a man of God, but certainly one of those of whom the Spirit of God says through the Apostle that they are in the futility of their mind, senseless, alienated from the life of God through the blindness of their heart. Since, then, by the Apostle's voice those who do the things you do are shown to be blinded in heart, with what face do you dare to say to those sound in heart and mind, "You have gone astray"—a deceiver saying to the truthful, "You are liars"? The Apostle says, "As the truth is in Jesus, put off, according to your former way of life, the old man, who is corrupted according to the desire of error, and be renewed in the spirit of your mind, and put on the new man, who has been created according to God in justice and holiness and truth. Putting away falsehood, let each one speak the truth with his neighbor." Where have you passed over these saving admonitions which the Apostle urges us to keep? For how could we have been found to have put off the old man and put on the new man, the one who is according to God? How could we have been seen remaining in justice and holiness and truth, we who, committing injustices with you, would have extinguished that new man, who is created according to God, and would have begun again to carry that old man, who is corrupted according to the desire of error, just as he was being corrupted before he began to know God? For all these things you do are done not by God's household but by the henchmen of Antichrist. "Putting away falsehood, let each one speak the truth with his neighbor, for we are members of one another." If you were one of the members of God's Church, believe me, you would never have brought a lie to the Church; but because you are the man of him who deceived Adam and Eve by his trickery, you brought a lie, in order to ensnare us just as the devil ensnared the first-formed human beings. You said: "Condemn Athanasius, because he has sinned gravely; otherwise you will be under the greatest guilt before God. Take up the faith of Arius, and you will live forever."

Hear what your dearest friend did with Adam and Eve as well, and you will find that you are now doing to us what he then did to them. "And they were both naked," says Moses in Genesis, "Adam and his wife, and they were not ashamed. Now the serpent was wiser than all the beasts that there were." And further on: "And the serpent said to the woman: Why has the Lord God said that you should not eat of every tree that is in paradise? And the woman said to the serpent: We shall eat of every tree that is in paradise, but of the fruit of the tree that is in the middle of paradise God said, You shall not eat of it, nor shall you touch it, lest you die." We say to you, who in the serpent's place are persuading us to condemn a man unheard and to slaughter an innocent one: The Lord has commanded that the innocent and the just are not to be killed. "And the serpent said to the woman: You will not die. For God knew that on whatever day you eat of it, your eyes will be opened, and you will be like gods, knowing good and evil." So this serpent, saying to us through you, "You will be more just if you shed just blood; you will be more blessed if you anathematize the apostolic and evangelical faith and take up the Arian perfidy" [...] is trampled underfoot, by God's grace, at least in you, by us who already know his deceit. But God is my witness that we grieve for you, because he has set himself up through you to ensnare us; for it is clear that back then he attacked Adam and Eve in his own person. I beg you not to take amiss what is said for the sake of your salvation. For I suppose you are pained that I have said the serpent attacked us through you, and that in many places I have placed you among those who were called serpents. Consider your work and theirs, and if you do not recognize that you are one body, then say that I speak unjustly. You certainly hear that your teachers in perfidy, the Jews, are often called serpents by the Lord in the holy Gospels: "Serpents, brood of vipers." Why did they deserve to be called by this name? Surely because of their wicked work, surely because of their unbelief. Hence John the Baptist too says to them: "Brood of vipers, who showed you how to flee from the wrath to come? Bear, then, fruits worthy of repentance." So just as some of them, those who believed in the only Son of God and corrected their ways, deserved to become sons of light, while the others are called serpents, so you too, unless you bear fruits worthy of repentance, unless you correct your ways, will be called the son of a viper and a serpent. For which of God's servants, seeing that you are a murderer and a blasphemer, would not call you by the name by which the Jews are called? Who among those who fear God will hesitate to declare what you are, when he sees that the scribes, Pharisees and rulers of the Jews are called serpents precisely because they shed the blood of the prophets and denied the only Son of God?

Since this is how things stand, it remains for you to do penance for your deeds, recognizing that God in his clemency has shown mercy to all who turn back from evil ways, and taking the Ninevites as your model; if you imitate them, you will surely obtain the help of mercy in the same way. Hear what was done regarding them, and what they themselves did, terrified by the preaching of Jonah. "The whale was commanded," says sacred Scripture, "and it cast Jonah up onto the land. And the word of the Lord came to Jonah a second time, saying: Arise and go to Nineveh, the great city, and preach in it according to the earlier message which I spoke to you. And Jonah arose and went to Nineveh, as the Lord had told him. Now Nineveh was a city so great that it took three days to cross. And Jonah began to enter the city, a day's journey, and he preached and said: Three days more, and Nineveh will be overthrown. And the men of Nineveh believed God, and they proclaimed a fast and clothed themselves in sackcloth, from the greatest of them to the least. And the word reached the king of Nineveh, and he rose from his throne, took off his robe, wrapped himself in sackcloth and sat on ashes. And it was proclaimed by the king of Nineveh and his magistrates, saying: Let neither men nor beasts nor cattle nor sheep taste anything; let them not eat, and let them not drink water. And the men wrapped themselves in sackcloth, and men and beasts cried out earnestly to God, and each turned back from his evil way and from the iniquity of his hands, saying: Who knows whether God will repent and turn from the wrath of his fury, and we shall not perish? And God saw their work, that each had turned back from his evil way. And God repented of the evil which he had said he would do to them, and he did not do it. And Jonah was grieved with a great grief and was confounded, and he prayed to God, saying: O Lord, were these not my words when I was still in my own land? That is why I hastened to flee to Tarshish, for I knew that you are compassionate and kind, patient and merciful, and relenting of evil." And further on: "And God said to Jonah: Are you greatly grieved over the gourd? I am greatly grieved, even to death. And the Lord said: You spared the gourd, for which you did not labor, nor did you make it grow, which sprang up in a night and perished in a night. And shall I not spare Nineveh, the great city, in which live more than a hundred and twenty thousand people who do not know their right hand from their left?" And as for you, Constantius: if God sees that you have cast off your wicked work, if he perceives that you have corrected your ruinous ways, and sees that you have been reformed in everything, believe me, you will begin to dwell in great happiness among the servants of God.

You also have the example of the most blessed apostle Paul. Perhaps, like him, you are doing these things in ignorance; if so, his example shows that as soon as you turn to confess the only Son of God, God will grant you pardon for your crimes as he granted it to him. Follow him, take his road, and listen to him speaking to the Philippians, telling who he was before he came to know Christ and how great a blessedness he was found worthy to gain after he knew him: “If anyone thinks he has grounds for confidence in the flesh, I have more: circumcised on the eighth day, of the race of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew born of Hebrews; as to the law, a Pharisee; as to zeal, a persecutor of the church; as to the righteousness that is in the law, I lived blameless. But whatever gains I had, these I counted as loss for Christ's sake. Indeed, I count everything as loss because of the surpassing worth of knowing Christ Jesus our Lord. For his sake I have suffered the loss of all things, and I count them as dung, so that I may gain Christ and be found in him, not having a righteousness of my own that comes from the law, but the one that comes through faith in Jesus Christ, the righteousness from God that rests on faith; so that I may know him and the power of his resurrection and the sharing of his sufferings, being conformed to his death, if somehow I may attain to his resurrection from the dead.” As has already been said, imitate him, follow him. He too was once what you are now, a persecutor of the church and a denier of the only Son of God; so may you be found to have turned in the same way to gain the heavenly kingdom, passing from faithlessness to embrace the catholic faith, and so crossing over from death to life. And hear further that he persecuted the church out of ignorance of God, as he reveals about himself to Timothy: “We know that the law is good, if one uses it lawfully, knowing this, that the law is not laid down for the righteous, but for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and sinners, for the wicked and profane, for those who kill their fathers and those who kill their mothers, for murderers, the sexually immoral, men who lie with men, kidnappers, liars, perjurers, and whatever else is contrary to sound teaching, in accordance with the gospel of the glory of the blessed God that was entrusted to me. I give thanks to him who strengthened me, Christ Jesus our Lord, because he judged me faithful and appointed me to his service, though I had formerly been a blasphemer, a persecutor and a man of violence. But I received mercy because I had acted ignorantly in unbelief, and the grace of our Lord overflowed for me with the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus.” So you too, once a persecutor, a man of violence and a blasphemer, can become blessed and truly most dear to God, if, like blessed Paul, you believe that Jesus Christ is the true Son of God; if you confess that he has always reigned with the Father and always will, that is, without beginning and without end; if you do not resist the sacred Scriptures when they proclaim that the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit have one eternity; and finally, if you believe that the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit have one Godhead. Believe me, you will then be in the company of the patriarchs, prophets, apostles and martyrs. Otherwise, when you begin to see yourself tormented with the devil and all his henchmen, you will blame yourself for having scorned these warnings of ours that would have saved you.
